sentences.zh: 志第二十五輿服

translations.literal: Treatise 25: Carriages and Vestments
translations.idiomatic: Treatise 25 — Carriages and Vestments

sentences.zh: 昔黃帝造車服，為之屏蔽，上古簡儉，未立等威。

translations.literal: In antiquity the Yellow Emperor fashioned chariots and garments to serve as a screen and barrier; in high antiquity simplicity prevailed, and gradations of dignity were not yet established.
translations.idiomatic: Long ago the Yellow Emperor devised chariots and dress as a protective screen; the remote past was austere, and ranks of ceremonial precedence had not yet been fixed.

sentences.zh: 而三、五之君，不相沿習，乃改正朔，易服色，車有輿輅之別，服有裘冕之差，文之以染繢，飾之以絺繡，華蟲象物，龍火分形，於是典章興矣。

translations.literal: Yet the rulers of the Three Sovereigns and Five Emperors did not carry on one another's usages; they revised the calendar and changed ceremonial colors. Chariots came to have distinctions of carriage and palanquin; garments came to have differences of fur robes and sacrificial caps. They were patterned with dyed and painted designs and adorned with fine embroidery—hua chong and symbolic creatures, dragon-and-fire motifs in separate forms—and thus the canon of rites arose.
translations.idiomatic: The sovereigns of the Three Sovereigns and Five Emperors, however, did not simply inherit one another's customs: each revised the calendar and altered ritual colors. Chariots were divided into carriage and palanquin grades; dress into fur robe and ceremonial cap. Dyed patterns, brocade ornament, hua-chong emblems and animal symbols, dragon and fire motifs in distinct forms—all this is how the ritual canon took shape.

sentences.zh: 周自夷王削弱，諸侯自恣。

translations.literal: From the time of King Yi of Zhou the house was weakened and the feudal lords did as they pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Once King Yi of Zhou had enfeebled the throne, the feudal lords began to act without restraint.

sentences.zh: 窮孔翬之羽毛，無以供其侈；

translations.literal: They exhausted the feathers of the kong and hui birds, yet still could not supply their extravagance;
translations.idiomatic: They stripped the forests of kong and hui plumage and still could not meet their extravagance;

sentences.zh: 極隨和之掌握，不足慊其華。

translations.literal: They exhausted the treasures held in the hands of Sui and He, yet still could not satisfy their love of splendor.
translations.idiomatic: They drained the legendary jades of Sui and He and still could not glut their appetite for display.

sentences.zh: 則皮弁革舄之容，非珠履鷸冠之玩也。

translations.literal: Then the appearance of leather caps and leather shoes was no longer the amusement of pearl slippers and yu-guan caps.
translations.idiomatic: Leather caps and buskins were no longer enough—courtiers wanted pearl slippers and yu-guan headdresses instead.

sentences.zh: 迨秦誅戰國，斟酌舊儀，則有鹵簿、金根、大駕、法駕，備千乘萬騎，異《舜典》、《周官》。

translations.literal: When Qin exterminated the Warring States and weighed the old rites, there were the imperial guard train, the golden-root carriage, the great escort, and the state escort, with a thousand chariots and ten thousand riders—differing from the Canon of Shun and the Offices of Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: After Qin destroyed the Warring States and sifted the former ritual code, it instituted the guard train, the golden-root carriage, the great escort, and the state escort—thousands of chariots and myriads of horsemen, unlike anything in the Canon of Shun or the Offices of Zhou.

sentences.zh: 漢氏因之，號乘輿三駕，儀衛之盛，無與比隆。

translations.literal: The Han adopted this, calling it the imperial carriage with three teams; the splendor of its guard and escort had no equal in grandeur.
translations.idiomatic: Han inherited the system, naming it the imperial carriage with three teams; no age matched the magnificence of its guard and escort.

sentences.zh: 東京帝王，博雅好古，明帝始令儒者考《曲臺》之說，依《周官》五輅六冕之文，山龍藻火之數，創為法服。

translations.literal: The Eastern capital emperors were broadly learned and fond of antiquity; Emperor Ming first ordered Confucian scholars to examine the explanations in the Quetai, and according to the text of the five chariots and six caps in the Offices of Zhou, and the numbers for mountain-dragon and flame patterns, created statutory vestments.
translations.idiomatic: The Eastern Han emperors were erudite and antiquarian; Emperor Ming first had scholars study the Quetai commentaries and, following the Offices of Zhou on the five chariots and six caps and the reckoning of mountain-dragon and flame motifs, drafted statutory dress.

sentences.zh: 雖有制作，竟寢不行。

translations.literal: Although there was fabrication, in the end it was shelved and not implemented.
translations.idiomatic: The garments were designed, but in the end the project was shelved and never carried out.

sentences.zh: 輿駕乘金根而已。

translations.literal: For imperial carriages they used only the golden-root carriage.
translations.idiomatic: In practice the throne rode only the golden-root carriage.

sentences.zh: 服則袞冕，冠則通天。

translations.literal: For dress they used the dragon robe; for caps the sky-reaching cap.
translations.idiomatic: Court dress meant the dragon robe; the crown meant the sky-reaching cap.

sentences.zh: 其後所御，多從袍服。

translations.literal: Thereafter what was actually worn was mostly robe and informal dress.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward emperors mostly wore robes and everyday dress.

sentences.zh: 事具前志。

translations.literal: The matter is set forth in the previous treatise.
translations.idiomatic: Details appear in the earlier treatise.

sentences.zh: 而裘冕之服，歷代不行。

translations.literal: Yet the fur robe and ceremonial cap were not used through the dynasties.
translations.idiomatic: The fur robe and sacrificial cap, however, were never consistently observed.

sentences.zh: 後魏、北齊，輿服奇詭，至隋氏一統，始復舊儀。

translations.literal: Later Wei and Northern Qi had bizarre chariots and vestments; only when the Sui unified the realm did the old rites begin to be restored.
translations.idiomatic: Northern Wei and Northern Qi produced outlandish carriages and dress; only after Sui reunified the empire were the old forms gradually revived.

sentences.zh: 隋制，車有四等，有亙幰、通幰、軺車、輅車。

translations.literal: Under Sui regulations, carriages had four grades: the full-canopy carriage, the open-canopy carriage, the light carriage, and the palanquin carriage.
translations.idiomatic: Sui statute divided carriages into four grades: full canopy, open canopy, light carriage, and palanquin.

sentences.zh: 初制五品以上乘偏幰車，其後嫌其不美，停不行用，以亙車代之。

translations.literal: At first officials of the fifth rank and above rode the partial-canopy carriage; later, finding it unattractive, its use was suspended and the full-canopy carriage was substituted.
translations.idiomatic: Initially fifth rank and above rode a partial-canopy carriage; when officials judged it unseemly, that type was abolished and the full-canopy carriage used instead.

sentences.zh: 三品以上通幰車，則青壁。

translations.literal: Officials of the third rank and above used the open-canopy carriage, with green side panels.
translations.idiomatic: Third rank and above took the open-canopy carriage with green side panels.

sentences.zh: 一品軺車，油幰朱網。

translations.literal: First rank used the light carriage, with oiled canopy and vermilion net.
translations.idiomatic: First rank used the light carriage with oiled canopy and vermilion netting.

sentences.zh: 唯輅車一等，聽敕始得乘之。

translations.literal: Only the palanquin grade might be ridden when an edict expressly permitted it.
translations.idiomatic: The palanquin grade alone required an imperial edict before one might ride it.

sentences.zh: 馬珂，一品以下九子，四品七子，五品五子。

translations.literal: Horse toggles: first rank and below had nine beads, fourth rank seven, fifth rank five.
translations.idiomatic: Bridle toggles: first rank and above nine beads; fourth rank seven; fifth rank five.

sentences.zh: 衣裳有常服、公服、朝服、祭服四等之制。

translations.literal: Garments had a system of four kinds: everyday dress, public dress, court dress, and sacrificial dress.
translations.idiomatic: Dress was organized into four categories: everyday, public, court, and sacrificial.

sentences.zh: 平巾幘，牛角箄簪，紫衫，白袍、靴，起梁帶。

translations.literal: The flat kerchief, ox-horn comb-pin, purple jacket, white robe and boots, and raised-belt sash.
translations.idiomatic: Everyday dress comprised the flat kerchief, ox-horn hairpin, purple jacket, white robe and boots, and raised belt.

sentences.zh: 五品已上，金玉鈿飾，用犀為簪，是為常服，武官盡服之。

translations.literal: Fifth rank and above added gold and jade inlay ornaments, using rhinoceros horn for the pin—this was everyday dress, and military officers all wore it.
translations.idiomatic: From fifth rank upward, gold and jade inlays appeared and rhinoceros horn served as the pin—this was everyday dress, worn by all military officers.

sentences.zh: 六品已下，衫以緋。

translations.literal: Sixth rank and below wore jackets in scarlet.
translations.idiomatic: Sixth rank and below wore scarlet jackets.

sentences.zh: 至於大仗陪立，五品已上及親侍加兩襠縢蛇，其勳侍去兩襠。

translations.literal: When standing attendance with the great halberds, fifth rank and above and personal attendants added double-breasted panels with serpent trim; meritorious attendants omitted the double panels.
translations.idiomatic: On grand halberd guard duty, fifth rank and above and personal attendants added double-breasted panels with serpent braid; meritorious attendants omitted the double panels.

sentences.zh: 弁冠，朱衣裳，素裳革帶，烏皮履，是為公服。

translations.literal: The bian cap, vermilion upper garment and plain lower garment, leather belt, and black leather shoes—this was public dress.
translations.idiomatic: Public dress was the bian cap, vermilion coat with plain skirt, leather belt, and black leather shoes.

sentences.zh: 其弁通用烏漆紗為之，象牙為簪導。

translations.literal: The bian was generally made of black lacquered gauze, with ivory pin guides.
translations.idiomatic: Bian caps were usually black lacquered gauze with ivory pin guides.

sentences.zh: 五品已上，亦以鹿胎為弁，犀為簪導者。

translations.literal: Fifth rank and above might also use deer-fetal for the cap and rhinoceros horn for the pin guide.
translations.idiomatic: Fifth rank and above might use deer fetal for the cap and rhinoceros horn for the guide.

sentences.zh: 加玉琪之飾：一品九琪，二品八琪，三品七琪，四品六琪。

translations.literal: Jade pendant ornaments were added: first rank nine pendants, second rank eight, third rank seven, fourth rank six.
translations.idiomatic: Jade finials were added by rank: nine for first, eight for second, seven for third, six for fourth.

sentences.zh: 三品兼有紛、鞶囊，佩於革帶之後，上加玉珮一。

translations.literal: Third rank and above also had sash tassels and leather pouches, worn behind the belt, with one jade pendant above.
translations.idiomatic: Third rank and above also wore sash tassels and leather pouches behind the belt, plus one jade pendant.

sentences.zh: 鞶囊：二品以上金縷，三品以上銀縷，五品以上䌽縷，文官尋常入內及在本司常服之。

translations.literal: Leather pouches: second rank and above gold thread, third rank and above silver thread, fifth rank and above colored thread—worn by civil officials when entering the palace or on routine duty in their offices.
translations.idiomatic: Pouches: second rank and above gold stitching; third rank and above silver; fifth rank and above colored thread—standard for civil officials in the palace or at their yamen.

sentences.zh: 親王，遠遊三梁冠，金附蟬，犀簪導，白筆。

translations.literal: Princes of the blood wore the far-travel cap with three beams, gold cicada attachment, rhinoceros pin guide, and white writing brush.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial princes wore the far-travel cap with three ridges, gold cicada finial, rhinoceros guide, and white brush.

sentences.zh: 三師三公、太子三師三少、尚書秘書二省、九寺、四監、太子三寺、諸郡縣關市、親王文學、籓王嗣王、公侯，進賢冠。

translations.literal: The Three Preceptors and Three Dukes, the Three Preceptors and Three Junior Tutors of the Heir Apparent, the two provinces of the Secretariat, the Nine Courts, the Four Directorates, the Heir Apparent's Three Courts, prefectures, counties, passes and markets, princely literary academies, enfeoffed kings, successor kings, dukes and marquises—all wore the advancement cap.
translations.idiomatic: The Three Preceptors and Three Dukes, the Heir Apparent's tutors, Secretariat and Chancellery, Nine Courts, Four Directorates, the Heir Apparent's Three Courts, prefectures and counties, passes and markets, princely literary institutes, enfeoffed and successor kings, dukes and marquises—all wore the advancement cap.

sentences.zh: 三品以上三梁，五品以上兩梁，犀簪導。

translations.literal: Third rank and above had three beams; fifth rank and above two beams, with rhinoceros pin guide.
translations.idiomatic: Third rank and above: three beams; fifth rank and above: two beams, with rhinoceros guide.

sentences.zh: 九品以上一梁，牛角簪導。

translations.literal: Ninth rank and above one beam, with ox-horn pin guide.
translations.idiomatic: Ninth rank and above: one beam, with ox-horn guide.

sentences.zh: 門下、內書、殿內三省，諸衛府，長秋監，太子左右庶子、內坊、諸率，宮門內坊，親王府都尉，府鎮防戍九品以上，散官一品已下，武弁幘。

translations.literal: The Gate Department, Secretariat, and Palace Department; the guard offices; the Directorate of the Palace Harem; the Heir Apparent's left and right aides, inner quarters, and guard rates; inner palace gates; princely commandants; garrison commanders of the ninth rank and above; and honorary officials of the first rank and below—all wore the military kerchief.
translations.idiomatic: Gate, Secretariat, and Palace departments; guard offices; Harem Directorate; Heir Apparent's aides, inner quarters, and guard rates; inner gates; princely commandants; frontier commanders of the ninth rank and above; honorary officials down to first rank—all wore the military kerchief.

sentences.zh: 侍中、中書令，加貂蟬，珮紫綬。

translations.literal: The Palace Attendant and Director of the Secretariat added the marten-tail cicada and wore the purple sash.
translations.idiomatic: The Palace Attendant and Director of the Secretariat added the marten cicada and purple sash.

sentences.zh: 散官者，白筆。

translations.literal: Honorary officials carried the white brush.
translations.idiomatic: Honorary officials carried the white brush.

sentences.zh: 御史、司隸二臺，。

translations.literal: The Censorate and the Directorate of Corrections.
translations.idiomatic: The Censorate and the Corrections Directorate.

sentences.zh: 謁者臺大夫以下，高山冠。

translations.literal: The Director of the Secretariat Gate and below wore the Gaoshan cap.
translations.idiomatic: The Secretariat Gate director and below wore the Gaoshan cap.

sentences.zh: 並絳紗單衣，白紗內單，皁領、褾、襈、裾，白練裙襦，絳蔽膝，革帶，金飾鈎䚢，方心曲領，紳帶，玉鏢金飾劍，亦通用金鏢，山玄玉佩，綬，韈，烏皮舄。

translations.literal: All wore crimson-gauze single coats, white gauze inner coats, black collars, cuffs, borders, and hems, white silk skirts and jackets, crimson knee covers, leather belts with gold hook plaques, square heart and curved collar, sash belt, jade-inlaid gold sword with gold plaque (gold plaque also used generally), dark mountain-pattern jade pendant, sash, socks, and black leather shoes.
translations.idiomatic: All wore crimson gauze outer coats, white gauze linings, black collar and trim, white silk skirts, crimson knee covers, leather belts with gold hooks, square heart and curved collar, sash, jade-inlaid gold sword (or gold plaque alone), dark mountain jade pendant, sash, socks, and black shoes.

sentences.zh: 是為朝服。

translations.literal: This was court dress.
translations.idiomatic: This constituted court dress.

sentences.zh: 玉佩，纁朱綬，施二玉環。

translations.literal: Jade pendant, xuan-vermilion sash, with two jade rings attached.
translations.idiomatic: Court dress included jade pendant and xuan-vermilion sash bearing two jade rings.

sentences.zh: 三品以上綠綬，四品、五品青綬。

translations.literal: Third rank and above used the green sash; fourth and fifth ranks the blue sash.
translations.idiomatic: Third rank and above wore the green sash; fourth and fifth the blue.

sentences.zh: 二品以下去玉環，六品以下去劍、珮、綬。

translations.literal: Second rank and below removed the jade rings; sixth rank and below removed sword, pendant, and sash.
translations.idiomatic: Second rank and below dropped the jade rings; sixth rank and below dropped sword, pendant, and sash.

sentences.zh: 八品以下，冠去白筆，衣省內單及曲領、蔽膝，著烏皮履。

translations.literal: Eighth rank and below removed the white brush from the cap, omitted the inner coat, curved collar, and knee covers, and wore only black leather shoes.
translations.idiomatic: Eighth rank and below removed the white brush, inner coat, curved collar, and knee covers, keeping only black shoes.

sentences.zh: 五品加紛、鞶囊。

translations.literal: Fifth rank added sash tassels and leather pouches.
translations.idiomatic: Fifth rank added sash tassels and pouches.

sentences.zh: 其綬纁朱者，用四䌽，赤、紅、縹、紺紅。

translations.literal: The xuan-vermilion sash used four colors: red, scarlet, light red, and dark red.
translations.idiomatic: The xuan-vermilion sash used four colors: red, scarlet, light red, and dark red.

sentences.zh: 朱質，纁文織，長一丈八尺，二百四十首，闊九寸。

translations.literal: Vermilion ground, xuan-pattern weave, one zhang eight chi long, two hundred forty strands, nine cun wide.
translations.idiomatic: Ground vermilion with xuan weave, length one zhang eight chi, two hundred forty strands, width nine cun.

sentences.zh: 綠綬用四䌽，綠、紫、黃、朱紅。

translations.literal: The green sash used four colors: green, purple, yellow, and vermilion-red.
translations.idiomatic: The green sash used green, purple, yellow, and vermilion-red.

sentences.zh: 綠質，長一丈八尺，二百四十首，闊九寸。

translations.literal: Green ground, length one zhang eight chi, two hundred forty strands, nine cun wide.
translations.idiomatic: Green ground, same length and strand count, nine cun wide.

sentences.zh: 紫綬用四䌽，紫、黃、赤、紅。

translations.literal: The purple sash used four colors: purple, yellow, red, and scarlet.
translations.idiomatic: The purple sash used purple, yellow, red, and scarlet.

sentences.zh: 紫質，長一丈六尺，一百八十首，闊八寸。

translations.literal: Purple ground, length one zhang six chi, one hundred eighty strands, eight cun wide.
translations.idiomatic: Purple ground, length one zhang six chi, one hundred eighty strands, eight cun wide.

sentences.zh: 青綬三䌽，白、青、紅。

translations.literal: The blue sash used three colors: white, blue, and red.
translations.idiomatic: The blue sash used white, blue, and red.

sentences.zh: 青質，長一丈四尺，一百四十首，闊七寸。

translations.literal: Blue ground, length one zhang four chi, one hundred forty strands, seven cun wide.
translations.idiomatic: Blue ground, length one zhang four chi, one hundred forty strands, seven cun wide.

sentences.zh: 玄衣纁裳冕而旒者，是為祭服，綬、珮、劍各依朝服之數。

translations.literal: Black upper garment and vermilion lower garment with tasselled cap—this was sacrificial dress; sash, pendant, and sword followed the numbers for court dress.
translations.idiomatic: Sacrificial dress was black coat, vermilion skirt, and tasselled cap; sash, pendant, and sword followed court-dress rules.

sentences.zh: 其章逢七品以下，降二為差，六品以下無章。

translations.literal: Emblem patches: from the seventh rank downward each rank dropped two grades; sixth rank and below had no emblems.
translations.idiomatic: Emblem patches descended by rank from seventh downward, two grades at a time; sixth rank and below wore none.

sentences.zh: 文武之官皆執笏，五品以上，用角牙為之，六品以下，用竹木。

translations.literal: Civil and military officials all carried tablets; fifth rank and above used horn and ivory, sixth rank and below bamboo or wood.
translations.idiomatic: All officials carried tablets—fifth rank and above horn or ivory, sixth rank and below bamboo or wood.

sentences.zh: 是時，內外群官，文物有序，僕禦清道，車服以庸。

translations.literal: At that time civil and military officials at court and in the provinces had ordered regalia; attendants cleared the way, and chariots and dress followed rank.
translations.idiomatic: Throughout the realm, officials' regalia was orderly; attendants swept the roads, and carriage and dress matched rank.

sentences.zh: 於是貴賤士庶，較然殊異。

translations.literal: Thus nobles and commoners, scholars and populace, were clearly distinct.
translations.idiomatic: Noble and humble, scholar and commoner, stood clearly apart.

sentences.zh: 越王侗於東都嗣位，下詔停廢。

translations.literal: When Prince Tong of Yue succeeded at the Eastern Capital, he issued an edict suspending and abolishing these regulations.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Tong of Yue took the throne at Luoyang, he ordered the system suspended.

sentences.zh: 自茲以後，浸以不章，以至於亡。

translations.literal: From then on it grew increasingly neglected, until the dynasty perished.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter observance faded until the state fell.

sentences.zh: 唐制，天子車輿有玉輅、金輅、象輅、革輅、木輅，是為五輅，耕根車、安車、四望車，已上八等，並供服乘之用。

translations.literal: Under Tang regulations the Son of Heaven's chariots included the jade palanquin, gold palanquin, ivory palanquin, leather palanquin, and wood palanquin—the five palanquins—plus the plough-root carriage, the secure carriage, and the four-views carriage; these eight grades above were all for the ruler's riding.
translations.idiomatic: Tang assigned the throne eight riding chariots: jade, gold, ivory, leather, and wood palanquins—the five palanquins—plus plough-root, secure, and four-views carriages.

sentences.zh: 其外有指南車、記裏鼓車、白鷺車、鸞旗車、辟惡車、軒車、豹尾車、羊車、黃鉞車，豹尾、黃鉞二車，武德中無，自貞觀已後加焉。

translations.literal: Besides these were the south-pointing carriage, the mile-drum carriage, the egret carriage, the luan-banner carriage, the evil-averting carriage, the xuan carriage, the leopard-tail carriage, the sheep carriage, and the yellow axe carriage; the leopard-tail and yellow axe carriages were absent in Wude and added from Zhenguan onward.
translations.idiomatic: Beyond them stood the south-pointing, mile-drum, egret, luan-banner, evil-averting, xuan, leopard-tail, sheep, and yellow-axe carriages; leopard-tail and yellow-axe were added after Zhenguan.

sentences.zh: 其黃鉞，天寶元年制改為金鉞。

translations.literal: The yellow axe carriage was renamed the gold axe carriage by statute in the first year of Tianbao.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianbao 1 the yellow-axe carriage was renamed the gold-axe carriage.

sentences.zh: 屬車十二乘，並為儀仗之用。

translations.literal: Twelve follow chariots served as ceremonial escort.
translations.idiomatic: Twelve follow chariots formed the ceremonial train.

sentences.zh: 大駕行幸，則分前後，施於鹵簿之內。

translations.literal: On great-escort journeys they were divided front and rear within the guard array.
translations.idiomatic: On imperial progresses they were split fore and aft within the guard array.

sentences.zh: 若大陳設，則分左右，施于儀衛之內。

translations.literal: When the great array was deployed, they were placed left and right within the ceremonial guard.
translations.idiomatic: In full ceremonial deployment they stood left and right within the guard.

sentences.zh: 玉輅，青質，以玉飾諸末。

translations.literal: The jade palanquin had a green body with jade ornaments on the extremities.
translations.idiomatic: The jade palanquin was green, jade-mounted at every extremity.

sentences.zh: 重輿，左青龍，右白虎，金鳳翅，畫虡文鳥獸，黃屋左纛。

translations.literal: Double carriage frame; azure dragon on the left, white tiger on the right; golden phoenix wings; painted mythical beasts; yellow canopy with left pennon.
translations.idiomatic: It had a double frame, azure dragon left and white tiger right, golden phoenix wings, painted mythical beasts, and a yellow canopy with left pennon.

sentences.zh: 金鳳一在軾前，十二鑾在衡，正縣鑾數，皆其副輅，及耕根則八。

translations.literal: One golden phoenix before the yoke; twelve tassels on the crossbar; the main row of tassels—with eight on the secondary palanquins and plough-root carriage.
translations.idiomatic: A golden phoenix sat before the yoke; twelve tassels hung on the crossbar—eight on secondary palanquins and the plough-root carriage.

sentences.zh: 二鈴在軾，龍輈前設鄣塵，青蓋黃裏，繡飾，博山鏡子，樹羽，輪皆朱班重牙。

translations.literal: Two bells on the yoke; dragon shafts with dust screens before; green canopy with yellow lining, embroidered trim, Boshan mirror bosses, feather standards, wheels with vermilion double-tooth rims.
translations.idiomatic: Two bells on the yoke, dragon shafts, dust screens, green canopy with yellow lining, embroidery, Boshan mirrors, feather standards, and vermilion double-tooth wheel rims.

sentences.zh: 左建旗十有二旒，皆畫升龍，其長曳地。

translations.literal: Left: a banner of twelve tassels, all painted ascending dragons, trailing to the ground.
translations.idiomatic: To the left, a twelve-tassel banner painted with ascending dragons, dragging on the ground.

sentences.zh: 右載闟戟，長四尺，廣三尺，黻文。

translations.literal: Right: a halberd rack, four chi long and three chi wide, with fu pattern.
translations.idiomatic: To the right, a halberd rack four chi by three, bearing fu pattern.

sentences.zh: 旗首金龍頭銜結綬及鈴綏。

translations.literal: The banner head was a golden dragon holding knotted cords and bell tassels.
translations.idiomatic: The banner head was a golden dragon clutching knotted cords and bell tassels.

sentences.zh: 駕蒼龍，金鍐方釳，插翟尾五焦，鏤錫，鞶纓十有二就。

translations.literal: Drawn by azure dragon horses; golden fang-shaped bits; five rows of pheasant-tail plumes on the shafts; carved tin; twelve tassel clusters on the bridle.
translations.idiomatic: Azure dragon teams drew it, with golden bits, five rows of pheasant-tail shaft plumes, carved tin, and twelve bridle clusters.

sentences.zh: 錫，馬當顱，鏤金為之。

translations.literal: Xi: horse forehead ornaments of carved gold.
translations.idiomatic: Xi ornaments were carved gold on the horses' foreheads.

sentences.zh: 鞶纓鞍皆以五䌽飾之。

translations.literal: Bridle and saddle were ornamented in five colors.
translations.idiomatic: Bridle and saddle used five-color ornament.

sentences.zh: 就，成也，一匝為一就也。

translations.literal: Jiu means "completed"; one circuit around the bridle counts as one jiu.
translations.idiomatic: Jiu means a full wrap; one circuit of the bridle counts as one jiu.

sentences.zh: 祭祀、納後則供之。

translations.literal: Supplied for sacrifices and when receiving the empress.
translations.idiomatic: It was used for sacrifices and when receiving the empress.

sentences.zh: 金輅，赤質，以金飾諸末，餘與玉輅同，駕赤昚，鄉射、祀還、飲至則供之。

translations.literal: The gold palanquin had a red body with gold ornaments on the extremities; otherwise like the jade palanquin; drawn by red horses; supplied for archery rites, returning from sacrifice, and the drinking ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: The gold palanquin was red with gold extremities, otherwise like the jade palanquin, drawn by red horses—for archery rites, post-sacrifice return, and the drinking ceremony.

sentences.zh: 象輅，黃質，以象飾諸末，餘與玉輅同，駕黃駵，行道則供之。

translations.literal: The ivory palanquin had a yellow body with ivory ornaments on the extremities; otherwise like the jade palanquin; drawn by yellow horses; supplied when traveling on the road.
translations.idiomatic: The ivory palanquin was yellow with ivory extremities, otherwise like the jade palanquin, drawn by yellow horses—for road travel.

sentences.zh: 革輅，白質，鞔之以革，餘與玉輅同，駕白駱，巡狩、臨兵事則供之。

translations.literal: The leather palanquin had a white body covered in leather; otherwise like the jade palanquin; drawn by white horses; supplied for inspection tours and military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The leather palanquin was white, leather-covered, otherwise like the jade palanquin, drawn by white horses—for tours and warfare.

sentences.zh: 木輅，黑質，漆之，餘與玉略同，駕黑駵，畋獵則供之。

translations.literal: The wood palanquin had a black body lacquered; otherwise like the jade palanquin; drawn by black horses; supplied for hunting.
translations.idiomatic: The wood palanquin was black lacquer, otherwise like the jade palanquin, drawn by black horses—for the hunt.

sentences.zh: 五輅之蓋，旌旗之質及鞶纓，皆從輅色，蓋之裏皆用黃。

translations.literal: The canopies of the five palanquins, the substance of banners and flags, and the bridle clusters all followed the palanquin color; the canopy lining was always yellow.
translations.idiomatic: Canopies, banner colors, and bridle clusters followed each palanquin's hue; lining was always yellow.

sentences.zh: 其鏤錫，五輅同。

translations.literal: The carved tin ornaments were the same on all five palanquins.
translations.idiomatic: Carved tin ornaments were identical on all five.

sentences.zh: 耕根車，青質，蓋三重，餘與玉輅同，耕籍則供之。

translations.literal: The plough-root carriage had a green body with a triple canopy; otherwise like the jade palanquin; supplied for ploughing the sacred field.
translations.idiomatic: The plough-root carriage was green with a triple canopy, otherwise like the jade palanquin, used for the sacred ploughing rite.

sentences.zh: 安車，金飾，重輿，曲壁，八鑾在衡，紫油纁，朱裏，通幰，朱絲絡網，朱鞶纓，朱覆閤朆，貝絡，駕赤駵，臨幸則供之。

translations.literal: The secure carriage had gold ornament, double frame, curved walls, eight tassels on the crossbar, purple oil and vermilion lining, open canopy, vermilion silk net, vermilion bridle clusters and covered flap, shell network; drawn by red horses; supplied when the emperor visited in person.
translations.idiomatic: The secure carriage was gold-trimmed with curved walls, eight crossbar tassels, purple oil and vermilion lining, open canopy, vermilion net and bridle, shell network, red horses—for personal imperial visits.

sentences.zh: 四望車，制同犢車，金飾。

translations.literal: The four-views carriage was made like the calf carriage with gold ornament.
translations.idiomatic: The four-views carriage followed the calf-carriage form with gold trim.

sentences.zh: 八鑾在衡，青油纁，朱裏，通幰，朱絲絡網，拜陵、臨吊則供之。

translations.literal: Eight tassels on the crossbar, green oil and vermilion lining, open canopy, vermilion silk net—supplied for tomb visits and condolence missions.
translations.idiomatic: Eight crossbar tassels, green oil and vermilion lining, open canopy, vermilion net—for tomb visits and condolence missions.

sentences.zh: 自高宗不喜乘輅，每有大禮，則御輦以來往。

translations.literal: From Emperor Gaozong, who disliked riding the palanquins, whenever there was a great rite he came and went by imperial litter instead.
translations.idiomatic: From Gaozong onward the throne disliked palanquins; at major rites the emperor traveled by litter instead.

sentences.zh: 爰洎則天以後，遂以為常。

translations.literal: From Empress Zetian onward this became the regular practice.
translations.idiomatic: After Empress Zetian it became routine.

sentences.zh: 玄宗又以輦不中禮，又廢而不用。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuanzong also found the litter contrary to ritual and abolished its use as well.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanzong judged the litter unritual and abolished it too.

sentences.zh: 開元十一年冬，將有事於南郊，乘輅而往，禮畢，騎而還。

translations.literal: In the winter of the eleventh year of Kaiyuan, when the southern suburb rite was imminent, he went out riding the palanquin and returned on horseback after the ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaiyuan 11 winter, before the southern suburb rite, he rode the palanquin out and returned on horseback.

sentences.zh: 自此行幸及郊祀等事，無遠近，皆騎于儀衛之內。

translations.literal: Thereafter for progresses and suburban sacrifices, near or far, he always rode within the guard.
translations.idiomatic: After that, for progresses and suburban rites, near or far, he always rode within the guard.

sentences.zh: 其五輅及腰輿之屬，但陳於鹵簿而已。

translations.literal: The five palanquins and waist-litters and the like were only arrayed in the guard train.
translations.idiomatic: The five palanquins and waist-litters were displayed only in the guard array.

sentences.zh: 皇后車則有重翟、厭翟、翟車、安車、四望車、金根車六等。

translations.literal: The empress's carriages comprised six grades: heavy di, pressed di, di carriage, secure carriage, four-views carriage, and golden-root carriage.
translations.idiomatic: The empress had six carriage grades: heavy di, pressed di, di carriage, secure carriage, four-views, and golden-root.

sentences.zh: 重翟車，青質，金飾諸末，輪畫朱，金根車牙，其箱飾以重翟羽，青油纁，朱裏通幰，繡紫帷，朱絲絡網，繡紫絡帶，八鑾在衡，鏤錫，鞶纓十二就，金鍐方釳，插翟尾，朱絲，駕蒼龍，受冊、從祀、享廟則供之。

translations.literal: The heavy-di carriage had a green body with gold ornaments on the extremities; wheels painted vermilion, golden-root carriage teeth; the box decorated with heavy-di feathers; green oil and vermilion lining, open canopy, embroidered purple curtains, vermilion silk net, embroidered purple net bands; eight tassels on the crossbar, carved tin, twelve bridle clusters, golden fang bits, pheasant-tail plumes on the shafts, vermilion silk; drawn by azure dragon horses; supplied when receiving the register, following sacrifice, or enjoying the ancestral temple.
translations.idiomatic: The heavy-di carriage was green with gold extremities, vermilion-painted wheels and golden-root teeth, its box trimmed with heavy-di feathers, green oil and vermilion lining, open canopy, purple embroidered curtains and net bands, eight crossbar tassels, carved tin, twelve bridle clusters, golden bits and pheasant-tail plumes, drawn by azure dragons—for investiture, collateral sacrifice, or temple offerings.

sentences.zh: 厭翟，赤質，金飾諸末，輪畫朱牙，其箱飾以次翟羽，紫油纁，朱裏通幰，紅錦帷，朱絲絡網，紅錦絡帶，余如重翟車。

translations.literal: The pressed-di carriage had a red body with gold ornaments on the extremities; wheels painted vermilion teeth; the box decorated with secondary-di feathers; purple oil and vermilion lining, open canopy, red brocade curtains, vermilion silk net, red brocade net bands—the rest like the heavy-di carriage.
translations.idiomatic: The pressed-di carriage was red with gold extremities, vermilion wheel teeth, secondary-di feather trim, purple oil and vermilion lining, red brocade curtains and net bands—otherwise matching the heavy-di carriage.

sentences.zh: 駕赤昚，采桑而供之。

translations.literal: Drawn by red horses; supplied when picking mulberry leaves.
translations.idiomatic: It was drawn by red horses and used for mulberry-picking rites.

sentences.zh: 翟車，黃質，金飾諸末，輪畫朱牙，其車側飾以翟羽，黃油纁，黃裏通幰，白紅錦帷，朱絲絡網，白紅錦絡帶，余如重翟。

translations.literal: The di carriage had a yellow body with gold ornaments on the extremities; wheels painted vermilion teeth; the sides decorated with di feathers; yellow oil and vermilion lining, open canopy, white-and-red brocade curtains, vermilion silk net, white-and-red brocade net bands—the rest like the heavy-di.
translations.idiomatic: The di carriage was yellow with gold extremities, di-feather side panels, yellow oil and vermilion lining, white-and-red brocade curtains—otherwise like the heavy-di.

sentences.zh: 駕黃昚，歸寧則供之。

translations.literal: Drawn by yellow horses; supplied when returning in peace to one's parents.
translations.idiomatic: Yellow horses drew it for the homeward visit to parents.

sentences.zh: 諸鞶纓之色，皆從車質。

translations.literal: The colors of all bridle clusters followed the carriage body color.
translations.idiomatic: Bridle-cluster colors always matched the carriage body.

sentences.zh: 安車，赤質，金飾，紫通幰朱裏。

translations.literal: The secure carriage had a red body with gold ornament and purple open canopy with vermilion lining.
translations.idiomatic: The empress's secure carriage was red with gold trim and a purple open canopy lined in vermilion.

sentences.zh: 駕四馬，臨幸及吊則供之。

translations.literal: Drawn by four horses; supplied on personal visits and condolence missions.
translations.idiomatic: Four horses drew it for imperial visits and condolence missions.

sentences.zh: 四望車，朱質，紫油通幰，油畫絡帶。

translations.literal: The four-views carriage had a vermilion body with purple oil open canopy and painted oil net bands.
translations.idiomatic: The four-views carriage was vermilion with purple-oil open canopy and painted net bands.

sentences.zh: 拜陵、臨吊則供之。

translations.literal: Supplied for tomb visits and condolence missions.
translations.idiomatic: It was used for tomb visits and condolence missions.

sentences.zh: 金根車，朱質，紫油通幰，油畫絡帶，朱絲網。

translations.literal: The golden-root carriage had a vermilion body with purple oil open canopy, painted oil net bands, and vermilion silk net.
translations.idiomatic: The golden-root carriage was vermilion with purple open canopy, painted net bands, and vermilion silk net.

sentences.zh: 常行則供之。

translations.literal: Supplied for routine travel.
translations.idiomatic: It served for everyday travel.

sentences.zh: 皇太子車輅，有金輅、軺車、四望車。

translations.literal: The Heir Apparent's chariots and palanquins comprised the gold palanquin, light carriage, and four-views carriage.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince had three grades: gold palanquin, light carriage, and four-views carriage.

sentences.zh: 金輅，赤質，金飾諸末，重較，箱畫虡文鳥獸，黃屋，伏鹿軾，龍輈，金鳳一在軾，前設鄣塵，朱蓋黃裏，輪畫朱牙，左建旗九旒，右載闟戟，旗首金龍頭銜結綬及鈴綏。

translations.literal: The gold palanquin had a red body with gold ornaments on the extremities, double rails, box painted with mythical beasts, yellow canopy, recumbent deer yoke, dragon shafts, one golden phoenix on the yoke, dust screen before, vermilion canopy with yellow lining, wheels painted vermilion teeth; left banner of nine tassels, right halberd rack; banner head a golden dragon holding knotted cords and bell tassels.
translations.idiomatic: The gold palanquin was red with gold extremities, double rails, beast-painted box, yellow canopy, recumbent-deer yoke, dragon shafts, golden phoenix, dust screen, vermilion canopy with yellow lining, nine-tassel banner left and halberd rack right, golden-dragon banner head.

sentences.zh: 駕赤昚四，八鑾在衡，二鈴在軾，金鍐方釳，插翟尾五焦，鏤錫，鞶纓九就。

translations.literal: Drawn by four red horses; eight tassels on the crossbar, two bells on the yoke, golden fang bits, five rows of pheasant-tail plumes, carved tin, nine bridle clusters.
translations.idiomatic: Four red horses drew it, with eight crossbar tassels, two yoke bells, golden bits, five pheasant-tail rows, carved tin, and nine bridle clusters.

sentences.zh: 從祀享、正冬大朝、納妃則供之。

translations.literal: Supplied for collateral sacrifice, the great winter court assembly, and receiving a consort.
translations.idiomatic: It was used for collateral sacrifice, the great winter audience, and consort investiture.

sentences.zh: 軺車，金飾諸末，紫幰幟朱裏，駕一馬。

translations.literal: The light carriage had gold ornaments on the extremities, purple canopy banners with vermilion lining, drawn by one horse.
translations.idiomatic: The light carriage had gold extremities, purple canopy with vermilion lining, and one horse.

sentences.zh: 五日常服及朝享宮臣、出入行道則供之。

translations.literal: Supplied for everyday dress on the five days, morning audiences with palace officials, and travel on the roads.
translations.idiomatic: It served for routine dress days, audiences with palace officials, and road travel.

sentences.zh: 四望車，金飾諸末，紫油纁，通幰朱裏，朱絲絡網，駕一馬。

translations.literal: The four-views carriage had gold ornaments on the extremities, purple oil and vermilion lining, open canopy with vermilion lining, vermilion silk net, drawn by one horse.
translations.idiomatic: The four-views carriage had gold extremities, purple oil and vermilion lining, open canopy, vermilion net, and one horse.

sentences.zh: 吊臨則供之。

translations.literal: Supplied for condolence missions.
translations.idiomatic: It was used for condolence missions.

sentences.zh: 王公已下車輅，親王及武職一品，象飾輅。

translations.literal: For chariots and palanquins of princes and dukes and below: princes of the blood and first-rank military posts used the ivory-decorated palanquin.
translations.idiomatic: Below the throne, princes and first-rank military officers used ivory-decorated palanquins.

sentences.zh: 自餘及二品、三品，革輅。

translations.literal: All others of the second and third ranks used the leather palanquin.
translations.idiomatic: Second and third ranks used leather palanquins.

sentences.zh: 四品，木輅。

translations.literal: Fourth rank: wood palanquin.
translations.idiomatic: Fourth rank: wood palanquin.

sentences.zh: 五品，軺車。

translations.literal: Fifth rank: light carriage.
translations.idiomatic: Fifth rank: light carriage.

sentences.zh: 象輅，以象飾諸末，朱班輪，八鑾在衡，左建旗，旗、畫龍，一升一降。

translations.literal: The ivory palanquin had ivory ornaments on the extremities, vermilion-rim wheels, eight tassels on the crossbar; left banner, banner and painting of dragons, one ascending and one descending.
translations.idiomatic: Ivory palanquins bore ivory extremities, vermilion wheel rims, eight crossbar tassels, and a left banner with ascending and descending dragons.

sentences.zh: 右載闟戟。

translations.literal: Right: halberd rack.
translations.idiomatic: To the right, a halberd rack.

sentences.zh: 革輅，以革飾諸末，左建旃，(通帛為旃，餘同象輅。

translations.literal: The leather palanquin had leather ornaments on the extremities; left banner a pennon (plain silk pennon; the rest like the ivory palanquin).
translations.idiomatic: Leather palanquins used leather extremities and a left plain-silk pennon; otherwise like the ivory palanquin.

sentences.zh: 木輅，以漆飾之，餘同革輅。

translations.literal: The wood palanquin was lacquered; the rest like the leather palanquin.
translations.idiomatic: Wood palanquins were lacquered; otherwise like leather palanquins.

sentences.zh: 軺車，曲壁，青通幰。

translations.literal: The light carriage had curved walls and green open canopy.
translations.idiomatic: Light carriages had curved walls and green open canopies.

sentences.zh: 諸輅皆朱質朱蓋，朱旗旃。

translations.literal: All palanquins had vermilion bodies, vermilion canopies, and vermilion banners and pennons.
translations.idiomatic: All palanquins used vermilion body, canopy, and banners.

sentences.zh: 一品九旒，二品八旒，三品七旒，四品六旒，其鞶纓就數皆准此。

translations.literal: First rank nine tassels, second rank eight, third rank seven, fourth rank six; bridle-cluster counts followed the same scale.
translations.idiomatic: Banner tassels and bridle clusters descended by rank: nine/eight/seven/six.

sentences.zh: 內命婦夫人乘厭翟車，嬪乘翟車，婕妤已下乘安車，各駕二馬。

translations.literal: Inner consorts of lady rank rode the pressed-di carriage; consorts rode the di carriage; talented ladies and below rode the secure carriage—each drawn by two horses.
translations.idiomatic: Inner court ladies rode pressed-di, consorts the di carriage, talented ladies and below the secure carriage—each with two horses.

sentences.zh: 外命婦、公主、王妃乘厭翟車，駕二馬。

translations.literal: Outer consorts, princesses, and princesses consort rode the pressed-di carriage, drawn by two horses.
translations.idiomatic: Outer consorts, princesses, and princesses consort used the pressed-di carriage with two horses.

sentences.zh: 自餘一品乘白銅飾犢車，青通幰，朱裏油纁，朱絲絡網，駕以牛。

translations.literal: All others of the first rank rode the white-bronze-decorated calf carriage with green open canopy, vermilion lining with oil finish, vermilion silk net, drawn by oxen.
translations.idiomatic: Other first-rank women used white-bronze calf carriages with green canopy, vermilion oil lining, vermilion net, and ox teams.

sentences.zh: 二品已下去油纁、絡網，四品青偏幰。

translations.literal: Second rank and below omitted oil finish and net; fourth rank used green partial canopy.
translations.idiomatic: Second rank and below dropped oil finish and net; fourth rank used a green partial canopy.

sentences.zh: 有唐已來，三公已下車輅，皆太僕官造貯掌。

translations.literal: Since the Tang dynasty, chariots and palanquins of the Three Dukes and below were all manufactured and stored by the Court of the Imperial Stud.
translations.idiomatic: From Tang times onward, palanquins for the Three Dukes and below were built and stored by the Imperial Stud.

sentences.zh: 若受制行冊命及二時巡陵、婚葬則給之。

translations.literal: They were issued when receiving edicts for investiture or seals, for biannual tomb visits, or for weddings and funerals.
translations.idiomatic: They were lent for investiture edicts, spring and autumn tomb visits, weddings, and funerals.

sentences.zh: 自此之後，皆騎馬而已。

translations.literal: After that everyone simply rode horses.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward everyone simply rode horses instead.

sentences.zh: 唐制，天子衣服，有大裘之冕、袞冕、鷩冕、毳冕、繡冕、玄冕、通天冠、武弁、黑介幘、白紗帽、平巾幘、白帢，凡十二等。

translations.literal: Under Tang regulations the Son of Heaven's garments comprised twelve grades: the great-fur cap, dragon robe, pheasant cap, feather cap, embroidery cap, dark cap, sky-reaching cap, military cap, black kerchief, white gauze cap, flat kerchief, and white headcloth.
translations.idiomatic: Tang assigned twelve imperial dress grades: great-fur, dragon, pheasant, feather, embroidery, and dark caps; sky-reaching, military, black kerchief, white gauze, flat kerchief, and white headcloth caps.

sentences.zh: 大裘冕，無旒，廣八寸，長一尺六寸，玄裘纁裏，已下廣狹准此。

translations.literal: The great-fur cap had no tassels, eight cun wide and one chi six cun long; black fur upper garment with vermilion lining—width and narrowness below followed this.
translations.idiomatic: The great-fur cap had no tassels, eight cun by one chi six; black fur coat with vermilion lining set the standard dimensions.

sentences.zh: 金飾，玉簪導，以組為纓，色如其綬。

translations.literal: Gold ornament, jade pin guide, sash tassel of cord colored like the sash.
translations.idiomatic: Gold trim and jade pin guide; cord tassel matching the sash color.

sentences.zh: 裘以黑羔皮為之，玄領、褾、襟緣。

translations.literal: The fur was made of black lamb fleece with black collar, cuffs, and border.
translations.idiomatic: The fur was black lamb fleece with black collar and trim.

sentences.zh: 朱裳，白紗中單，皁領，青褾、襈、裾、革帶，玉鈎、䚢，大帶，蔽漆隨裳。

translations.literal: Vermilion skirt, white gauze inner coat, black collar, green cuffs, borders, and hem, leather belt with jade hooks, great belt, knee cover of lacquered leather following the skirt.
translations.idiomatic: Vermilion skirt, white gauze lining, black collar, green trim, leather belt with jade hooks, great belt, and lacquered knee cover.

sentences.zh: 鹿盧玉具劍，火珠鏢首。

translations.literal: Deer-hoof jade sword fittings, fire-pearl sword plaque.
translations.idiomatic: Deer-hoof jade sword mount and fire-pearl plaque.

sentences.zh: 請改從素服，以會禮文。

translations.literal: "We ask that it be changed to plain dress to accord with ritual text."
translations.idiomatic: "We ask that plain dress replace it to align with the classics."

sentences.zh: 」制從之。

translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved.

translations.literal: In the winter of the eleventh year of Kaiyuan, when Xuanzong was about to sacrifice at the southern suburb, Director of the Secretariat Zhang Yue memorialized again, saying: "According to the statute, when the emperor sacrifices to the Supreme God of Heaven he wears the great-fur cap—this comes from the Rites of Zhou and values simplicity."

translations.literal: On the first and fifteenth of the month and when conducting affairs, it was also worn.
translations.idiomatic: Also worn on first- and fifteenth-day audiences and when conducting state affairs.

sentences.zh: 進德冠，九琪，加金飾，其常服及白練裙襦通著之。

translations.literal: Advancing Virtue cap, nine studs, gold ornament added, worn together with everyday dress and white silk skirt and blouse.
translations.idiomatic: The Advancing Virtue cap bore nine studs with gold ornament and was worn with everyday dress and white silk skirt and blouse.

sentences.zh: 若服袴褶，則與平巾幘通著。

translations.literal: If wearing trousers and riding robe, it was worn together with the plain kerchief cap.
translations.idiomatic: With trousers and riding robe, it was paired with the plain kerchief cap.

sentences.zh: 自永徽已後，唯服袞冕、具服、公服而已。

translations.literal: From the Yonghui era onward, only dragon cap, full dress, and court dress were worn.
translations.idiomatic: After Yonghui, only dragon cap, full dress, and court dress remained in use.

sentences.zh: 若乘馬袴，則著進德冠，自餘並廢。

translations.literal: If riding in horse trousers, then the Advancing Virtue cap was worn; all the rest were abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: Horseback riding required the Advancing Virtue cap; everything else was abolished.

sentences.zh: 若宴服、常服，紫衫袍與諸王同。

translations.literal: For banquet dress and everyday dress, the purple coat and robe were the same as those of the princes.
translations.idiomatic: Banquet and everyday dress used the same purple coat and robe as the princes.

sentences.zh: 開元二十六年，肅宗升為皇太子，受冊，太常所撰儀注有服絳紗袍之文。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year of Kaiyuan, Suzong was elevated to Crown Prince and received investiture; the rites protocol composed by the Court of Imperial Sacrifices contained text about wearing a crimson gauze robe.
translations.idiomatic: Kaiyuan 26, when Suzong was invested as Crown Prince, the Court of Imperial Sacrifices protocol prescribed a crimson gauze robe.

sentences.zh: 太子以為與皇帝所稱同，上表辭不敢當，請有以易之。

translations.literal: The Crown Prince thought it was the same as what the emperor was called, submitted a memorial declining and not daring to accept, and requested a substitute.
translations.idiomatic: The Crown Prince judged the name identical to the emperor's and memorialized that he dared not accept it, asking for a substitute.

sentences.zh: 玄宗令百官詳議。

translations.literal: Xuanzong ordered the hundred officials to deliberate in detail.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanzong ordered a full deliberation by the officials.

sentences.zh: 尚書左丞相裴耀卿、太子太師蕭嵩等奏曰：「謹按《衣服令》，皇太子具服，有遠遊冠，三梁，加金附蟬九首，施珠翠，黑介幘，髪纓綏，犀簪導，絳紗袍，白紗中單，皁領、褾、襈，白裙襦，方心曲領，絳紗蔽膝，革帶，劍，珮，綬等，謁廟還宮、元日冬至朔日入朝、釋奠則服之。

translations.literal: Left Director of the Department of State Affairs Pei Yaoqing, Grand Preceptor of the Crown Prince Xiao Song, and others memorialized: "We have carefully examined the Vestments Statute. The Crown Prince's full dress includes the far-wandering cap, three ridges, gold attached cicada nine heads, pearl and kingfisher ornament, black cap undercap, hair tassel cord, rhinoceros-horn pin guide, crimson gauze robe, white gauze inner coat, black collar, cuffs, and borders, white skirt and blouse, square heart and curved collar, crimson gauze knee cover, leather belt, sword, pendant, sash, and the like; it is worn when visiting temples and returning to the palace, entering court on New Year's Day, the winter solstice, and the first of the month, and at the school sacrifice."
translations.idiomatic: Pei Yaoqing, Xiao Song, and others replied: "The Vestments Statute defines the Crown Prince's full dress—far-wandering three-ridge cap with nine gold cicada ornaments, pearls and kingfisher feathers, black cap undercap, hair tassel, rhinoceros-horn pin guide, crimson gauze robe, white gauze lining, black trim, white skirt and blouse, square heart and curved collar, crimson knee cover, belt, sword, pendant, and sash—for temple visits, New Year, winter solstice, first-of-month audiences, and the school sacrifice."

sentences.zh: 其絳紗袍則是冠衣之內一物之數，與裙襦、劍、珮等無別。

translations.literal: The crimson gauze robe is merely one item among the cap and garments, no different from skirt and blouse, sword, pendant, and the like.
translations.idiomatic: The crimson gauze robe is only one component of the full ensemble, no different from skirt and blouse, sword, or pendant.

sentences.zh: 至於貴賤之差，尊卑之異，則冠為首飾，名制有殊，並珠旒及裳䌽章之數，多少有別，自外不可事事差異。

translations.literal: As for differences between noble and base, honored and lowly, the cap is the head ornament and its name and form differ; pearl tassels and the number of skirt color chapters also differ. Apart from these, not every item can differ.
translations.idiomatic: Rank distinctions belong chiefly to the cap—its name, form, pearl tassels, and emblem count on the skirt. Other garments need not differ item by item.

sentences.zh: 亦有上下通服，名制是同，禮重則具服，禮輕則從省。

translations.literal: There are also garments shared by superior and inferior, with the same name and form; when the rite is weighty full dress is worn, when light it is simplified.
translations.idiomatic: Some garments are shared across ranks under the same name; weighty rites require full dress, lighter ones permit simplification.

sentences.zh: 今以至敬之情，有所未敢，衣服不可減省，稱謂須更變名。

translations.literal: Now, out of utmost reverence, there is something not yet dared; the garments cannot be reduced, but the designation must be changed.
translations.idiomatic: Out of deepest reverence the Crown Prince dares not accept the name; the garments need not be cut back, but the title must change.

sentences.zh: 望所撰儀注，不以絳紗袍為稱，但稱為具服，則尊卑有差，謙光成德。

translations.literal: We hope the composed rites protocol will not use crimson gauze robe as the designation, but only call it full dress; then noble and base will have distinction, and humility and virtue will be accomplished.
translations.idiomatic: Let the protocol name the garment full dress rather than crimson gauze robe, preserving rank difference and the Crown Prince's humility.

sentences.zh: 」議奏上，手敕改為朱明服，下所司行用焉。

translations.literal: The deliberation was submitted; an imperial handwritten decree changed it to Vermilion Bright dress and sent it down to the offices for implementation.
translations.idiomatic: Their report was accepted; the emperor by handwritten decree renamed it Vermilion Bright dress and ordered its use.

sentences.zh: 《武德令》，侍臣服有袞、鷩、毳、繡、玄冕，及爵弁，遠遊、進賢冠，武弁，獬豸冠，凡十等。

translations.literal: Wude Statute: Attendant ministers' dress had dragon, pheasant, feather, embroidered, and dark caps, also noble cap, far-wandering and advancing worth caps, military cap, and unicorn cap—ten grades in all.
translations.idiomatic: The Wude Statute defined ten grades of ministerial dress: dragon, pheasant, feather, embroidered, and dark caps, noble cap, far-wandering and advancing worth caps, military cap, and unicorn cap.

sentences.zh: 袞冕，垂青珠九旒，以組為纓，色如其綬，青纊充耳，簪導。

translations.literal: Dragon cap: nine dangling green pearl tassels, cord tassel colored like the sash, green cotton ear plugs, pin guide.
translations.idiomatic: The dragon cap bore nine dangling green pearl tassels, a matching cord tassel, green ear plugs, and pin guide.

sentences.zh: 青衣，纁裳，服九章。

translations.literal: Green upper garment, vermilion lower garment, nine emblem chapters.
translations.idiomatic: Green coat and vermilion skirt bore nine emblem chapters.

sentences.zh: 白紗中單，黼領，青褾、襈裙。

translations.literal: White gauze inner coat, fu collar, green cuffs and bordered skirt.
translations.idiomatic: White gauze lining, fu collar, and green cuffs and bordered skirt.

sentences.zh: 革帶，鈎䚢，大帶，黻，劍，珮，綬，朱韈，赤舄，第一品服之。

translations.literal: Leather belt, hook buckle, great belt, fu pattern, sword, pendant, sash, vermilion socks, red shoes; first rank wore it.
translations.idiomatic: Leather belt, hook buckle, great belt, fu pattern, sword, pendant, sash, vermilion socks, and red shoes—worn by first rank.

sentences.zh: 鷩冕，七旒，服七章，餘同袞冕，第二品服之。

translations.literal: Pheasant cap: seven tassels, seven emblem chapters; the rest like the dragon cap; second rank wore it.
translations.idiomatic: The pheasant cap had seven tassels and seven emblem chapters; otherwise like the dragon cap—worn by second rank.

sentences.zh: 毳冕，五旒，服五章，餘同鷩冕，第三品服之。

translations.literal: Feather cap: five tassels, five emblem chapters; the rest like the pheasant cap; third rank wore it.
translations.idiomatic: The feather cap had five tassels and five chapters; otherwise like the pheasant cap—worn by third rank.

sentences.zh: 繡冕，四旒，服三章，餘並同毳冕，第四品服之。

translations.literal: Embroidered cap: four tassels, three emblem chapters; all the rest like the feather cap; fourth rank wore it.
translations.idiomatic: The embroidered cap had four tassels and three chapters; otherwise like the feather cap—worn by fourth rank.

sentences.zh: 玄冕，衣無章，裳刻黻一章，餘同繡冕，第五品服之。

translations.literal: Dark cap: upper garment without emblem chapters, skirt carved with one fu chapter; the rest like the embroidered cap; fifth rank wore it.
translations.idiomatic: The dark cap had an unmarked coat and a skirt with one carved fu emblem; otherwise like the embroidered cap—worn by fifth rank.

sentences.zh: 爵弁，玄纓，簪導，青衣，纁裳，白紗中單，青領、褾、裙，革帶，鈎䚢，大帶，爵韠，韈，赤履，九品已上服之。

translations.literal: Noble cap: dark tassel, pin guide, green upper garment, vermilion lower garment, white gauze inner coat, green collar, cuffs, and skirt, leather belt, hook buckle, great belt, noble knee cover, socks, red shoes; ninth rank and above wore it.
translations.idiomatic: The noble cap bore a dark tassel and pin guide, green coat and vermilion skirt, white gauze lining with green trim, leather belt, hook buckle, great belt, noble knee cover, socks, and red shoes—worn by ninth rank and above.

sentences.zh: 凡冕服，助祭及親迎若私家祭祀皆服之，爵弁亦同。

translations.literal: For all cap dress, assisting at sacrifice, welcoming a bride in person, or private family sacrifice—all wore it; the noble cap likewise.
translations.idiomatic: Cap dress was worn for assisting at sacrifice, personal bride-welcome, and private family rites; the noble cap followed the same rule.

sentences.zh: 凡冕，制皆以羅為之，其服以紬。

translations.literal: For all caps, the form was made of gauze; the garments were of pongee.
translations.idiomatic: All ceremonial caps were gauze; their garments were pongee.

sentences.zh: 爵弁用紬為之，其服用繒。

translations.literal: The noble cap was made of pongee; its garments were of thick silk.
translations.idiomatic: The noble cap was pongee; its garments were thick silk.

sentences.zh: 遠遊三梁冠，黑介幘，青綏。

translations.literal: Far-wandering three-ridge cap, black cap undercap, green cord.
translations.idiomatic: Far-wandering three-ridge cap with black cap undercap and green cord.

sentences.zh: 皆諸王服之，親王則加金附蟬。

translations.literal: All princes wore it; imperial princes added gold attached cicada.
translations.idiomatic: All princes wore it; imperial princes added the gold cicada ornament.

sentences.zh: 進賢冠，三品以上三梁，五品以上兩梁，九品以上一梁。

translations.literal: Advancing worth cap: three ridges for third rank and above, two ridges for fifth rank and above, one ridge for ninth rank and above.
translations.idiomatic: The advancing worth cap had three ridges from third rank up, two from fifth rank up, and one from ninth rank up.

sentences.zh: 皆三公、太子三師三少、五等爵、尚書省、秘書省、諸寺監學、太子詹事府、三寺及散官，親王師友、文學、國官，若諸州縣關津嶽瀆等流內九品以上服之。

translations.literal: All Three Excellencies, the Crown Prince's three masters and three juniors, five noble ranks, the Department of State Affairs, Secretariat, various directorates, schools, Crown Prince's household office, three courts and unsalaried offices, imperial princes' mentors, companions, literary instructors, and state officials, and also officials of ninth rank and above in prefectures, counties, passes, fords, sacred peaks, rivers, and the like within the regular hierarchy wore it.
translations.idiomatic: It was worn by Three Excellencies, the Crown Prince's tutors, nobles of five ranks, central secretariats and directorates, Crown Prince's household, princely staff, state officials, and ninth-rank officials in prefectures, counties, passes, and river shrines.

sentences.zh: 武弁，平巾幘，皆武官及門下、中書、殿中、內侍省、天策上將府、諸衛領軍武候監門、領左右太子諸坊諸率及鎮戍流內九品已上服之。

translations.literal: Military cap and plain kerchief cap: all military officers and the Gate Secretariat, Secretariat, Palace Administration, Inner Service Directorate, Heavenly Stratagem General's Office, various guards, army supervisors, gate guards, Left and Right Commands, Crown Prince's various compounds and rate commands, and garrison officials of ninth rank and above within the regular hierarchy wore them.
translations.idiomatic: Military cap and plain kerchief cap were worn by military officers, palace guards, secretariats, Inner Service, guard commands, Crown Prince's household guards, and garrison officials of ninth rank and above.

sentences.zh: 其親王府佐九品以上，亦准此。

translations.literal: Princely household aides of ninth rank and above also followed this rule.
translations.idiomatic: Princely aides of ninth rank and above followed the same rule.

sentences.zh: 法冠，一名獬豸冠，以鐵為柱，其上施珠兩枚，為獬豸之形。

translations.literal: Law cap, also called unicorn cap, with iron pillars above which two pearls were set in the form of a unicorn.
translations.idiomatic: The law cap, also called the unicorn cap, had iron posts topped with two pearls shaped like a unicorn.

sentences.zh: 左右御史臺流內九品以上服之。

translations.literal: Officials of ninth rank and above within the regular hierarchy of the Left and Right Censorate wore it.
translations.idiomatic: Censorate officials of ninth rank and above wore it.

sentences.zh: 高山冠者，內侍省內謁者及親王下司閤等服之。

translations.literal: The Lofty Mountain cap was worn by inner attendants of the Inner Service Directorate and princes' gate stewards and the like.
translations.idiomatic: The Lofty Mountain cap was worn by Inner Service attendants and princes' gate stewards.

sentences.zh: 卻非冠者，亭長、門僕服之。

translations.literal: The Repelling Wrong cap was worn by pavilion chiefs and gate servants.
translations.idiomatic: The Repelling Wrong cap was worn by pavilion chiefs and gate servants.

sentences.zh: 諸應冠而未冠者，並雙童髻，空頂幘。

translations.literal: All who should wear a cap but had not yet been capped wore double child topknots and open-top kerchief caps.
translations.idiomatic: Those not yet capped wore double child topknots and open-top kerchief caps.

sentences.zh: 五品已上雙玉導，金飾，三品以上加寶飾，六品以下無飾。

translations.literal: Fifth rank and above had double jade guides with gold ornament; third rank and above added gem ornament; sixth rank and below had no ornament.
translations.idiomatic: From fifth rank up, double jade pin guides bore gold ornament; from third rank up, gem ornament was added; sixth rank and below had none.

sentences.zh: 朝服，冠，幘，纓，簪導，絳紗單衣，白紗中單，皁領、襈、裙，白裙襦，革帶，鈎䚢，假帶，曲領方心，絳紗蔽膝，韈，舄，劍，珮，綬。

translations.literal: Court dress: cap, kerchief, tassel, pin guide, crimson gauze single coat, white gauze inner coat, black collar, borders, and skirt, white skirt and blouse, leather belt, hook buckle, imitation belt, curved collar and square heart, crimson gauze knee cover, socks, shoes, sword, pendant, sash.
translations.idiomatic: Court dress comprised cap, kerchief, tassel, pin guide, crimson gauze coat, white gauze lining, black trim, white skirt and blouse, leather belt, hook buckle, imitation belt, curved collar and square heart, crimson knee cover, socks, shoes, sword, pendant, and sash.

sentences.zh: 一品已下，五品以下，陪祭、朝饗、拜表大事則服之。

translations.literal: First rank and below, fifth rank and above wore it for assisting at sacrifice, court banquets, and presenting memorials on great affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Ranks one through five wore it for assisting at sacrifice, court banquets, and major memorial presentations.

sentences.zh: 七品已上，去劍、珮、綬，餘並同。

translations.literal: Seventh rank and above removed sword, pendant, and sash; all the rest was the same.
translations.idiomatic: From seventh rank up, sword, pendant, and sash were omitted; otherwise the dress was the same.

sentences.zh: 公服，冠，幘，纓，簪導，絳紗單衣，白裙襦，革帶，鈎䚢，假帶，方心，韈，履，粉，鞶囊。

translations.literal: Court dress: cap, kerchief, tassel, pin guide, crimson gauze single coat, white skirt and blouse, leather belt, hook buckle, imitation belt, square heart, socks, shoes, sash, pouch.
translations.idiomatic: Court dress comprised cap, kerchief, tassel, pin guide, crimson gauze coat, white skirt and blouse, leather belt, hook buckle, imitation belt, square heart, socks, shoes, sash, and pouch.

sentences.zh: 一品以下，五品以上，謁見東宮及餘公事則服之。

translations.literal: First rank and below, fifth rank and above wore it when visiting the Eastern Palace and for other official business.
translations.idiomatic: Ranks one through five wore it for audiences with the Crown Prince and other official business.

sentences.zh: 其六品以下，去紛、鞶囊，餘並同。

translations.literal: Sixth rank and below removed sash and pouch; all the rest was the same.
translations.idiomatic: From sixth rank down, sash and pouch were omitted; otherwise the dress was the same.

sentences.zh: 諸珮綬者，皆雙綬。

translations.literal: All who wore pendant sashes had double sashes.
translations.idiomatic: All pendant sashes were double.

sentences.zh: 親王纁朱綬，四䌽，赤、黃，縹、紺。

translations.literal: Imperial princes: vermilion-red sash, four colors—red, yellow, light blue, and dark blue.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial princes wore a vermilion-red sash in four colors—red, yellow, light blue, and dark blue.

sentences.zh: 純朱質，纁文織。

translations.literal: Pure vermilion body, vermilion-pattern weave.
translations.idiomatic: Pure vermilion ground with vermilion-pattern weave.

sentences.zh: 長一丈八尺，二百四十首，廣九寸。

translations.literal: One zhang eight chi long, two hundred forty strands, nine cun wide.
translations.idiomatic: One zhang eight chi long, two hundred forty strands, nine cun wide.

sentences.zh: 一品綠綟綬，四䌽，紫、黃、赤。

translations.literal: First rank: green sash, four colors—purple, yellow, and red.
translations.idiomatic: First rank wore a green sash in four colors—purple, yellow, and red.

sentences.zh: 純綠質，長一丈八尺，二百四十首，廣九寸。

translations.literal: Pure green body, one zhang eight chi long, two hundred forty strands, nine cun wide.
translations.idiomatic: Pure green ground, one zhang eight chi long, two hundred forty strands, nine cun wide.

sentences.zh: 二品、三品紫綬，三䌽，紫、黃、赤。

translations.literal: Second and third ranks: purple sash, three colors—purple, yellow, and red.
translations.idiomatic: Second and third ranks wore a purple sash in three colors—purple, yellow, and red.

sentences.zh: 純紫質。

translations.literal: Pure purple body.
translations.idiomatic: Pure purple ground.

sentences.zh: 長一丈六尺，一百八十首，廣八寸。

translations.literal: One zhang six chi long, one hundred eighty strands, eight cun wide.
translations.idiomatic: One zhang six chi long, one hundred eighty strands, eight cun wide.

sentences.zh: 四品青綬，三䌽，青、白、紅。

translations.literal: Fourth rank: green sash, three colors—green, white, and red.
translations.idiomatic: Fourth rank wore a green sash in three colors—green, white, and red.

sentences.zh: 純青質。

translations.literal: Pure green body.
translations.idiomatic: Pure green ground.

sentences.zh: 長一丈四尺，一百四十首，廣七寸。

translations.literal: One zhang four chi long, one hundred forty strands, seven cun wide.
translations.idiomatic: One zhang four chi long, one hundred forty strands, seven cun wide.

sentences.zh: 五品黑綬，二䌽，青、紺。

translations.literal: Fifth rank: black sash, two colors—green and dark blue.
translations.idiomatic: Fifth rank wore a black sash in two colors—green and dark blue.

sentences.zh: 純紺質。

translations.literal: Pure dark blue body.
translations.idiomatic: Pure dark blue ground.

sentences.zh: 長一丈二尺，一百首，廣六寸。

translations.literal: One zhang two chi long, one hundred strands, six cun wide.
translations.idiomatic: One zhang two chi long, one hundred strands, six cun wide.

sentences.zh: 有綬者則有紛，皆長六尺四寸，廣二尺四分，各隨綬色。

translations.literal: Those with sashes also had fen sashes, all six chi four cun long and two chi four cun wide, each following the sash color.
translations.idiomatic: Sash wearers also wore matching fen sashes six chi four cun long and two chi four cun wide.

sentences.zh: 諸鞶囊，二品以上金縷，三品金銀鏤，四品銀鏤，五品䌽鏤。

translations.literal: All pouches: second rank and above gold thread, third rank gold and silver openwork, fourth rank silver openwork, fifth rank colored openwork.
translations.idiomatic: Pouches were gold-threaded from second rank up, gold-and-silver openwork for third rank, silver openwork for fourth, and colored openwork for fifth.

sentences.zh: 諸珮，一品珮山玄玉，二品以下、五品以上，佩水蒼玉。

translations.literal: All pendants: first rank wore mountain dark jade pendant; second rank and below, fifth rank and above wore water azure jade pendant.
translations.idiomatic: First rank wore mountain dark jade; ranks two through five wore water azure jade.

sentences.zh: 諸文官七品以上朝服者，簪白筆，武官及爵則不簪。

translations.literal: All civil officials of seventh rank and above in court dress pinned the white brush; military officers and nobles did not pin it.
translations.idiomatic: Civil officials of seventh rank and above in court dress pinned the white brush; military officers and nobles did not.

sentences.zh: 諸舄履並烏色，舄重皮底，履單皮底。

translations.literal: All shoes and boots were black; shoes had double leather soles, boots single leather soles.
translations.idiomatic: All footwear was black; court shoes had double leather soles, boots single leather soles.

sentences.zh: 諸勳官及爵任職事官者，正衣本服，自外各從職事服。

translations.literal: Meritorious officials and nobles holding substantive offices wore their proper rank dress; all others followed the dress of their substantive office.
translations.idiomatic: Meritorious nobles in substantive posts wore their rank dress; others followed their active office.

sentences.zh: 諸致仕及以理去官，被召謁見，皆服前官從省服。

translations.literal: All retired officials and those who left office by rule, when summoned for audience, wore the simplified dress of their former office.
translations.idiomatic: Retired officials and those who left office properly wore their former rank's simplified dress when summoned.

sentences.zh: 平巾幘，簪箄導，冠支，五品以上紫褶，六品以下緋褶，加兩襠縢虵，並白袴，起梁帶。

translations.literal: Plain kerchief cap, hairpin pie pin guide, cap brace, purple riding robe for fifth rank and above, scarlet riding robe for sixth rank and below, add double-crotch garter snake, all white trousers, raised-ridge belt.
translations.idiomatic: Plain kerchief cap with pie pin guide and cap brace; fifth rank and above wore purple riding robe, sixth and below scarlet, with double-crotch garter snake, white trousers, and raised-ridge belt.

sentences.zh: 鞾，武官及衛官陪立大仗則服之。

translations.literal: Boots: military officers and guard officers standing with the great guard wore them.
translations.idiomatic: Boots were worn by military and guard officers on grand guard duty.

sentences.zh: 若文官乘馬，亦通服之，去兩襠縢虵。

translations.literal: If civil officials rode horses, they also generally wore them, removing the double-crotch garter snake.
translations.idiomatic: Civil officials on horseback wore the same dress minus the double-crotch garter snake.

sentences.zh: 諸視品府佐，武弁，平巾幘。

translations.literal: Adjunct-rank prefectural aides: military cap, plain kerchief cap.
translations.idiomatic: Adjunct-rank prefectural aides wore military cap and plain kerchief cap.

sentences.zh: 國官，進賢一梁冠，黑介幘，簪導。

translations.literal: State officials: advancing worth one-ridge cap, black cap undercap, pin guide.
translations.idiomatic: State officials wore the advancing worth one-ridge cap with black cap undercap and pin guide.

sentences.zh: 其服各准正品，參朝則服之。

translations.literal: Their garments each followed the substantive rank; they wore them when attending court.
translations.idiomatic: Their dress matched the substantive rank and was worn at court audiences.

sentences.zh: 若謁見府公，府佐平巾黑幘，國官黑介幘，皆白紗單衣，烏皮履。

translations.literal: If visiting the prefect, prefectural aides wore plain kerchief black cap, state officials black cap undercap, all with white gauze single coat and black leather shoes.
translations.idiomatic: When visiting the prefect, aides wore plain kerchief with black cap and state officials black cap undercap, all in white gauze coat and black leather shoes.

sentences.zh: 諸流外官行署，三品以上黑介幘，絳公服，方心，革帶，鈎䚢，假帶，韈，烏皮履。

translations.literal: All outside-the-regular-hierarchy officials in field offices: third rank and above black cap undercap, crimson court dress, square heart, leather belt, hook buckle, imitation belt, socks, black leather shoes.
translations.idiomatic: Field officials outside the regular hierarchy from third rank up wore black cap undercap, crimson court dress, square heart, leather belt, hook buckle, imitation belt, socks, and black leather shoes.

sentences.zh: 九品以上絳褠衣，去方心、假帶，餘同絳公服。

translations.literal: Ninth rank and above: crimson gōu robes, removing square heart and imitation belt; the rest same as crimson court dress.
translations.idiomatic: From ninth rank up, officials wore crimson gōu robes without square heart or imitation belt; otherwise the dress matched crimson court dress.

sentences.zh: 其非行署者，太常寺謁者、卜博士、醫助教、祝史、贊引，鴻臚寺掌儀、諸典書、典學，內侍省內典引，太子門下坊典儀、內坊導客舍人、諸贊者，王公以下舍人，公主謁者等，各准行署，依品服。

translations.literal: Those not in field offices—Court of Imperial Sacrifices ushers, divination masters, medical assistants, invocators, eulogists, Court of State Ceremonial ritual directors, all record keepers and academy instructors, Palace Domestic Service inner ushers, Crown Prince's Household ritual directors, inner quarters guest guides and attendants, all eulogists, attendants of princes and below, princess ushers, and the like—each followed field-office standards and dressed by rank.
translations.idiomatic: Officials outside field offices—including ushers, diviners, medical assistants, invocators, eulogists, ritual directors, record keepers, academy instructors, palace ushers, crown prince household staff, princely attendants, and princess ushers—followed field-office dress by rank.

sentences.zh: 自外及民任雜掌無官品者，皆平巾幘，緋衫，大口袴。

translations.literal: Those outside and commoners holding miscellaneous posts without official rank all wore plain kerchief cap, scarlet coat, and wide-leg trousers.
translations.idiomatic: Commoners and outsiders in miscellaneous posts without official rank wore plain kerchief cap, scarlet coat, and wide-leg trousers.

sentences.zh: 朝集從事則服之。

translations.literal: Court assembly clerks wore them.
translations.idiomatic: Court assembly clerks wore this dress.

sentences.zh: 諸典謁，武弁，絳公服。

translations.literal: All ceremonial ushers: military cap, crimson court dress.
translations.idiomatic: Ceremonial ushers wore military cap and crimson court dress.

sentences.zh: 其齋郎，介幘，褠衣。

translations.literal: Acolytes: cap undercap, gōu robes.
translations.idiomatic: Acolytes wore cap undercap and gōu robes.

sentences.zh: 自外品子任雜掌者，皆平巾幘，緋衫，大口袴。

translations.literal: Those from outside whose sons of rank held miscellaneous posts all wore plain kerchief cap, scarlet coat, and wide-leg trousers.
translations.idiomatic: Outsiders whose sons of rank held miscellaneous posts wore plain kerchief cap, scarlet coat, and wide-leg trousers.

sentences.zh: 朝集從事則服之。

translations.literal: Court assembly clerks wore them.
translations.idiomatic: Court assembly clerks wore this dress.

sentences.zh: 黑介幘，簪導，深衣，青褾、領，革帶，烏皮履。

translations.literal: Black cap undercap, pin guide, deep garments, green cuffs and collar, leather belt, black leather shoes.
translations.idiomatic: They wore black cap undercap and pin guide, deep garments with green cuffs and collar, leather belt, and black leather shoes.

sentences.zh: 未冠則雙童髻，空頂黑介幘，去革帶。

translations.literal: If not yet capped: double youth topknot, open-top black cap undercap, remove leather belt.
translations.idiomatic: Before capping, they wore double youth topknots and open-top black cap undercap, without leather belt.

sentences.zh: 國子、太學、四門學生參見則服之。

translations.literal: Students of the Directorate, Imperial University, and Four Gates Academy wore them when attending audiences.
translations.idiomatic: Directorate, Imperial University, and Four Gates students wore this dress at audiences.

sentences.zh: 書算學生、州縣學生，則烏紗帽，白裙襦，青領。

translations.literal: Calligraphy and arithmetic students and prefectural and county students wore black gauze cap, white skirt and blouse, and green collar.
translations.idiomatic: Calligraphy, arithmetic, and local students wore black gauze cap, white skirt and blouse, and green collar.

sentences.zh: 諸外官拜表受詔皆服。

translations.literal: All field officials wore them when submitting memorials or receiving edicts.
translations.idiomatic: Field officials wore this dress when submitting memorials or receiving edicts.

sentences.zh: 其餘公事及初上，並公服。

translations.literal: For other official business and first court appearance, court dress.
translations.idiomatic: For other official business and first court appearance, they wore court dress.

sentences.zh: 諸州大中正，進賢一梁冠，絳紗公服，若有本品者，依本品參朝服之。

translations.literal: All state great rectifiers: advancing worth one-ridge cap, crimson gauze court dress; if they held substantive rank, they dressed by that rank at court.
translations.idiomatic: State great rectifiers wore advancing worth one-ridge cap and crimson gauze court dress; those with substantive rank dressed accordingly at court.

sentences.zh: 諸州縣佐史、鄉正、里正、岳瀆祝史、齋郎，並介幘，絳褠衣。

translations.literal: All prefectural and county clerks, village heads, ward heads, mountain-and-river invocators, and acolytes all wore cap undercap and crimson gōu robes.
translations.idiomatic: Prefectural and county clerks, village and ward heads, mountain-and-river invocators, and acolytes wore cap undercap and crimson gōu robes.

sentences.zh: 平巾幘，緋褶，大口袴，紫附褠，尚食局主食、典膳局主食、太官署食官署掌膳服之。

translations.literal: Plain kerchief cap, scarlet riding robe, wide-leg trousers, purple attached gōu—worn by chief food officers of the Board of Imperial Viands, chief food officers of the Board of Ceremonial Banquets, and kitchen directors of the Grand and Palace Food Offices.
translations.idiomatic: Chief food officers of the imperial kitchens wore plain kerchief cap, scarlet riding robe, wide-leg trousers, and purple attached gōu.

sentences.zh: 平巾綠幘，青布袴，尚食局主膳、典膳局典食、太官署食官署供膳服之。

translations.literal: Plain kerchief with green cap, blue cloth trousers—worn by food stewards of the Board of Imperial Viands, food stewards of the Board of Ceremonial Banquets, and food suppliers of the Grand and Palace Food Offices.
translations.idiomatic: Kitchen stewards and food suppliers wore plain kerchief with green cap and blue cloth trousers.

sentences.zh: 平巾五辮髻，青袴褶，青耳屩，羊車小史服之。

translations.literal: Plain kerchief with five-braid topknot, blue riding robe and trousers, blue ear slippers—worn by goat-cart attendants.
translations.idiomatic: Goat-cart attendants wore plain kerchief with five-braid topknot, blue riding robe and trousers, and blue ear slippers.

sentences.zh: 總角髻，青袴褶，漏刻生、漏童服之。

translations.literal: Total-angle topknot, blue riding robe and trousers—worn by clepsydra attendants and water-clock boys.
translations.idiomatic: Clepsydra attendants and water-clock boys wore total-angle topknot with blue riding robe and trousers.

sentences.zh: 龍朔二年九月戊寅，司禮少常伯孫茂道奏稱：「諸臣九章服，君臣冕服，章數雖殊，飾龍名袞，尊卑相亂。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, day wuyin, of the second year of Longshuo, Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices Sun Maodao memorialized: "The nine-pattern robes of ministers and the miǎn robes of ruler and subject, though differing in emblem count, all use dragon ornament and are called dragon robes, confusing high and low."
translations.idiomatic: On wuyin day in the ninth month of Longshuo 2, Vice Director Sun Maodao reported that ministers' nine-pattern robes and imperial miǎn robes, though differing in emblem count, all bore dragon ornament called dragon robes, blurring rank.

sentences.zh: 望諸臣九章衣以雲及麟代龍，升山為上，仍改冕。

translations.literal: He hoped ministers' nine-pattern robes would use clouds and qilin in place of dragons, elevate mountains to the top, and also revise the miǎn.
translations.idiomatic: He proposed replacing dragons on ministers' nine-pattern robes with clouds and qilin, placing mountains foremost, and revising the miǎn accordingly.

sentences.zh: 」當時紛議不定。

translations.literal: " At the time debate was unsettled.
translations.idiomatic: Debate at the time remained unsettled.

sentences.zh: 儀鳳年，太常博士蘇知機又上表，以公卿以下冕服，請別立節文。

translations.literal: In the Yifeng era, Erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices Su Zhiji again submitted a memorial concerning miǎn robes for dukes and ministers and below, requesting separate ritual specifications.
translations.idiomatic: During Yifeng, Erudite Su Zhiji again petitioned for separate ritual rules governing miǎn robes for dukes, ministers, and lower ranks.

sentences.zh: 敕下有司詳議。

translations.literal: An imperial order was issued for the relevant offices to deliberate in detail.
translations.idiomatic: The throne ordered the relevant offices to deliberate in detail.

sentences.zh: 崇文館學士校書郎楊炯奏議曰；

translations.literal: Academician of the Chongwen Hall and Collator Yang Jiong submitted a memorial stating:
translations.idiomatic: Chongwen Hall academician and collator Yang Jiong replied:

sentences.zh: 古者太昊庖犧氏，仰以觀象，俯以察法，造書契而文籍生。

translations.literal: In antiquity the Great Bright Fuxi looked upward to observe the heavens and downward to discern patterns, created writing and tallies, and written records arose.
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity Fuxi the Great Bright looked up to read the heavens and down to read the patterns of earth, invented writing and tallies, and written records were born.
