sentences.zh: 次有黃帝軒轅氏，長而敦敏，成而聰明，垂衣裳而天下理。

translations.literal: Next came the Yellow Emperor Xuanyuan, reverent and quick in youth, wise in maturity, who draped his robes and the realm was governed.
translations.idiomatic: Then came the Yellow Emperor Xuanyuan—reverent and quick as a youth, wise in maturity—who draped his robes and brought order to the realm.

sentences.zh: 其後數遷五德，君非一姓。

translations.literal: Afterward the Five Phases shifted repeatedly and rulers were not of one surname.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter dynasties cycled through the Five Phases and rulers changed surnames.

sentences.zh: 體國經野，建邦設都，文質所以再而復，正朔所以三而改。

translations.literal: Organizing the state and mapping the realm, founding domains and establishing capitals—ritual substance and ornament alternated twice, and the calendar was changed thrice.
translations.idiomatic: As states were organized, domains founded, and capitals established, ritual form alternated twice and the calendar was changed three times.

sentences.zh: 夫改正朔者，謂夏後氏建寅，殷人建醜，周人建子。

translations.literal: As for changing the calendar: the Xia used yin as the first month, the Shang used chou, the Zhou used zi.
translations.idiomatic: Changing the calendar meant the Xia began the year in yin, the Shang in chou, and the Zhou in zi.

sentences.zh: 至於以日系月，以月系時，以時系年，此則三王相襲之道也。

translations.literal: As for linking days to months, months to seasons, and seasons to years—this was the way the Three Dynasties handed down rule.
translations.idiomatic: Linking days to months, months to seasons, and seasons to years was the calendar tradition handed down by the Three Dynasties.

sentences.zh: 夫易服色者，謂夏後氏尚黑，殷人尚白，周人尚赤。

translations.literal: As for changing ceremonial colors: the Xia favored black, the Shang white, the Zhou red.
translations.idiomatic: Changing ceremonial colors meant the Xia favored black, the Shang white, and the Zhou red.

sentences.zh: 至於山、龍、華蟲、宗彝、藻、火、粉米、黼、黻，此又百代可知之道也。

translations.literal: As for mountains, dragons, pheasants, ritual vessels, water plants, fire, grain, axe, and opposing chevrons—this too was a tradition knowable across a hundred generations.
translations.idiomatic: The emblems of mountain, dragon, pheasant, ritual vessel, water plant, fire, grain, axe, and opposing chevrons were likewise traditions legible across a hundred generations.

sentences.zh: 謹按《虞書》曰：「予欲觀古人之象，日、月、星辰、山、龍、華蟲作繪，宗彝、藻、火、粉米、黼、黻絺繡。

translations.literal: I respectfully note that the Book of Yu says: "I wish to observe the images of the ancients: sun, moon, stars, mountains, dragons, and pheasants painted; ritual vessels, water plants, fire, grain, axe, and opposing chevrons embroidered."
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Yu says: "I wish to observe the images of antiquity—sun, moon, stars, mountains, dragons, and pheasants painted; ritual vessels, water plants, fire, grain, axe, and opposing chevrons embroidered."

sentences.zh: 」由此言之，則其所從來者尚矣。

translations.literal: " From this it follows that their origin is exceedingly ancient.
translations.idiomatic: From this it follows that the tradition is exceedingly ancient.

sentences.zh: 夫日月星辰者，明光照下土也。

translations.literal: Sun, moon, and stars illuminate the earth below.
translations.idiomatic: Sun, moon, and stars represent bright light shining upon the earth.

sentences.zh: 山者，布散雲雨，象聖王澤沾下人也。

translations.literal: Mountains scatter clouds and rain, symbolizing the sage king's bounty reaching the people below.
translations.idiomatic: Mountains scatter clouds and rain, symbolizing how the sage king's bounty reaches the people.

sentences.zh: 龍者，變化無方，象聖王應機布教也。

translations.literal: Dragons transform without fixed form, symbolizing the sage king's responsive teaching according to circumstance.
translations.idiomatic: Dragons transform without fixed form, symbolizing the sage king's teaching in response to circumstance.

sentences.zh: 華蟲者，雉也，身被五采，象聖王體兼文明也。

translations.literal: The pheasant emblem is the pheasant; its body bears five colors, symbolizing the sage king's embodiment of both civil and martial virtue.
translations.idiomatic: The pheasant emblem is the pheasant itself, its five-colored plumage symbolizing the sage king's union of civil and martial virtue.

sentences.zh: 宗彝者，武蜼也，以剛猛制物，象聖王神武定亂也。

translations.literal: The ritual vessel emblem is the martial lizard; by fierce strength it subdues things, symbolizing the sage king's divine martial quelling of disorder.
translations.idiomatic: The ritual vessel emblem is the martial lizard, whose fierce strength subdues chaos and symbolizes the sage king's divine martial power.

sentences.zh: 藻者，逐水上下，象聖王隨代而應也。

translations.literal: Water plants rise and fall with the water, symbolizing the sage king's response to each age.
translations.idiomatic: Water plants rise and fall with the water, symbolizing the sage king's responsiveness to each age.

sentences.zh: 火者，陶冶烹飪，象聖王至德日新也。

translations.literal: Fire smelts and cooks, symbolizing the sage king's supreme virtue renewed daily.
translations.idiomatic: Fire smelts and cooks, symbolizing the sage king's ever-renewing supreme virtue.

sentences.zh: 米者，人恃以生，象聖王物之所賴也。

translations.literal: Grain is what people rely on to live, symbolizing what the sage king provides for all things.
translations.idiomatic: Grain sustains human life, symbolizing what the sage king provides for all living things.

sentences.zh: 黼能斷割，象聖王臨事能決也。

translations.literal: The axe can cut and decide, symbolizing the sage king's ability to decide affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The axe cuts and decides, symbolizing the sage king's decisive judgment in affairs of state.

sentences.zh: 黻者，兩己相背，象君臣可否相濟也。

translations.literal: Opposing chevrons show two forms back to back, symbolizing minister and ruler aiding each other through assent and dissent.
translations.idiomatic: Opposing chevrons show two forms back to back, symbolizing how minister and ruler aid each other through assent and dissent.

sentences.zh: 逮有周氏，乃以日月星辰為旌旗之飾，又登龍於山，登火于宗彝，於是乎制袞冕以祀先王也。

translations.literal: When the Zhou arose, they used sun, moon, and stars as banner ornament, placed dragons upon mountains and fire upon ritual vessels, and thus established dragon robes to sacrifice to former kings.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Zhou, sun, moon, and stars adorned banners; dragons were set upon mountains and fire upon ritual vessels—and thus dragon robes were established for sacrifice to former kings.

sentences.zh: 九章者，法于陽數也。

translations.literal: The nine patterns follow the yang number.
translations.idiomatic: The nine patterns follow the number of yang.

sentences.zh: 以龍為首章者，袞者卷也，龍德神異，應變潛見，表聖王深沈遠智，卷舒神化也。

translations.literal: Taking dragon as the first pattern: dragon robe means "rolled"; the dragon's virtue is divine and strange, responding to change while hidden or revealed, expressing the sage king's deep and far-reaching wisdom, rolling and unrolling in divine transformation.
translations.idiomatic: Dragon as the first pattern: "dragon robe" means "rolled robe"; the dragon's divine strangeness, responding to change while hidden or revealed, expresses the sage king's deep wisdom and divine transformation.

sentences.zh: 又制鷩冕以祭先公也。

translations.literal: They also established pheasant miǎn to sacrifice to former lords.
translations.idiomatic: They also established pheasant miǎn for sacrifice to former lords.

sentences.zh: 鷩者雉也，有耿介之志，表公有賢才，能守耿介之節也。

translations.literal: The pheasant has an upright and resolute will, expressing that lords possess worthy talent and can uphold upright integrity.
translations.idiomatic: The pheasant's upright and resolute will expresses that lords possess worthy talent and uphold integrity.

sentences.zh: 又制毳冕以祭四望也。

translations.literal: They also established feather miǎn to sacrifice to the Four Sacred Peaks.
translations.idiomatic: They also established feather miǎn for sacrifice to the Four Sacred Peaks.

sentences.zh: 四望者，嶽瀆之神也。

translations.literal: The Four Sacred Peaks are the spirits of mountains and rivers.
translations.idiomatic: The Four Sacred Peaks are the spirits of mountains and rivers.

sentences.zh: 武蜼者，山林所生也，明其象也。

translations.literal: The martial lizard is born in mountain forests; this makes clear its emblematic meaning.
translations.idiomatic: The martial lizard dwells in mountain forests, making clear its emblematic meaning.

sentences.zh: 制絺冕以祭社稷也。

translations.literal: They established fine-silk miǎn to sacrifice to the altars of soil and grain.
translations.idiomatic: They established fine-silk miǎn for sacrifice at the altars of soil and grain.

sentences.zh: 社稷，土穀之神也。

translations.literal: Soil and grain are the spirits of earth and harvest.
translations.idiomatic: Soil and grain are the spirits of earth and harvest.

sentences.zh: 粉米由之成也，象其功也。

translations.literal: Ground grain is formed from them, symbolizing their achievement.
translations.idiomatic: Ground grain is formed from them, symbolizing their sustaining power.

sentences.zh: 又制玄冕以祭群小祀也。

translations.literal: They also established dark miǎn to sacrifice at lesser rites.
translations.idiomatic: They also established dark miǎn for lesser rites.

sentences.zh: 百神異形，難可遍擬，但取黻之相背異名也。

translations.literal: The hundred spirits take different forms and cannot all be depicted; one takes only the opposing chevrons' back-to-back difference in name.
translations.idiomatic: The hundred spirits take different forms and cannot all be depicted; only the opposing chevrons' back-to-back form is taken as their emblem.

sentences.zh: 夫以周公之多才也，故化定制禮，功成作樂。

translations.literal: Because the Duke of Zhou was so abundantly talented, when culture was settled he fixed ritual, and when achievement was complete he composed music.
translations.idiomatic: Because the Duke of Zhou was abundantly talented, when culture was settled he fixed ritual, and when achievement was complete he composed music.

sentences.zh: 夫以孔宣之將聖也，故行夏之時，服周之冕。

translations.literal: Because Confucius was nearly sage, he followed the Xia calendar and wore the Zhou miǎn.
translations.idiomatic: Because Confucius was nearly sage, he followed the Xia calendar and wore Zhou miǎn.

sentences.zh: 先王之法服，乃此之自出矣；

translations.literal: The ritual garments of former kings issued from this;
translations.idiomatic: The ritual garments of former kings issued from this;

sentences.zh: 天下之能事，又於是乎畢矣。

translations.literal: and the realm's fullest accomplishment was thereby complete.
translations.idiomatic: and the realm's fullest accomplishment was thereby complete.

sentences.zh: 今表狀「請制大明冕十二章，乘輿服之」者。

translations.literal: Now the memorial states: "Request establishment of Grand Bright miǎn with twelve patterns, for the imperial carriage to wear."
translations.idiomatic: The memorial now proposes a Grand Bright miǎn with twelve patterns for the emperor.

sentences.zh: 謹按，日月星辰者，已施旌旗矣；

translations.literal: I respectfully note: sun, moon, and stars are already applied to banners;
translations.idiomatic: Sun, moon, and stars already adorn imperial banners;

sentences.zh: 龍武山火者，又不逾于古矣。

translations.literal: dragon, martial emblem, mountain, and fire do not exceed antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: and dragon, martial emblem, mountain, and fire do not exceed ancient precedent.

sentences.zh: 而雲麟鳳有四靈之名，玄龜有負圖之應，雲有紀官之號，水有感德之祥，此蓋別表休征，終是無逾比象。

translations.literal: Yet cloud, qilin, and phoenix have the names of the Four Auspicious Beings; the dark tortoise has the response of bearing the chart; cloud has the title of a recorded office; water has the omen of responsive virtue—these merely express separate auspicious signs and ultimately do not exceed comparable emblems.
translations.idiomatic: Yet cloud, qilin, and phoenix bear the names of the Four Auspicious Beings; the dark tortoise bears the chart; cloud has a recorded office; water has an omen of responsive virtue—these express separate auspicious signs and do not exceed comparable emblems.

sentences.zh: 然則皇王受命，天地與興符，仰觀則璧合珠連，俯察則銀黃玉紫。

translations.literal: When the sovereign receives Heaven's mandate, Heaven and Earth join in issuing tokens; looking up one sees jade disks and pearls joined, looking down one sees silver, gold, and purple jade.
translations.idiomatic: When the sovereign receives Heaven's mandate, Heaven and Earth unite in issuing tokens—jade disks and pearls joined above, silver, gold, and purple jade below.

sentences.zh: 盡南宮之粉壁，不足寫其形狀；

translations.literal: Exhaust the whitewashed walls of the Southern Palace and they cannot depict all their forms;
translations.idiomatic: Not even the whitewashed walls of the Southern Palace could depict all their forms;

sentences.zh: 罄東觀之鉛黃，無以紀其名實。

translations.literal: empty all the ink of the Eastern Pavilion and it cannot record their names and substance.
translations.idiomatic: nor could all the ink of the Eastern Pavilion record their names and substance.

sentences.zh: 固不可畢陳於法服也。

translations.literal: They certainly cannot all be displayed on ritual garments.
translations.idiomatic: They certainly cannot all be displayed on ritual garments.

sentences.zh: 雲也者，從龍之氣也，水也者，藻之自生也，又不假別為章目也。

translations.literal: Cloud is the qi that follows the dragon; water is what water plants grow from of themselves—they need no separate emblem categories.
translations.idiomatic: Cloud is the qi that follows the dragon; water is what water plants grow from—they need no separate emblem categories.

sentences.zh: 此蓋不經之甚也。

translations.literal: This is exceedingly unreasonable.
translations.idiomatic: This is exceedingly unreasonable.

sentences.zh: 又「鸞冕八章，三公服之」者。

translations.literal: Again: "Luan miǎn with eight patterns, for the Three Dukes to wear."
translations.idiomatic: Again: "Luan miǎn with eight patterns for the Three Dukes."

sentences.zh: 鸞者，太平之瑞也，非三公之德也。

translations.literal: The luan is an omen of great peace, not the virtue of the Three Dukes.
translations.idiomatic: The luan is an omen of great peace, not the virtue of the Three Dukes.

sentences.zh: 鷹鸇者，鷙鳥也，適可以辨祥刑之職也。

translations.literal: The hawk eagle is a fierce bird, suitable to represent the office of discerning auspicious punishment.
translations.idiomatic: The hawk eagle is a fierce bird suited to the office of discerning auspicious punishment.

sentences.zh: 熊羆者，猛獸也，適可以旌武臣之力也。

translations.literal: The bear is a fierce beast, suitable to honor the strength of military officers.
translations.idiomatic: The bear is a fierce beast suited to honoring military officers' strength.

sentences.zh: 又稱藻為水草，無所法象，引張衡賦雲，「蒂倒茄於藻井，披江葩之狎獵。

translations.literal: They also call water plants mere water grasses with no symbolic model, citing Zhang Heng's rhapsody on clouds: "Stalks inverted eggplants in the ceiling well, rippling river blossoms in close array."
translations.idiomatic: They also call water plants mere water grasses with no symbolic model, citing Zhang Heng's rhapsody: "Stalks inverted eggplants in the ceiling well, rippling river blossoms in close array."

sentences.zh: 」謂為蓮花，取其文采者。

translations.literal: " They call them lotus flowers, taking their patterned brilliance.
translations.idiomatic: They call these lotus flowers, taking their patterned brilliance.

sentences.zh: 夫茄者蓮也，若以蓮花代藻，變古從今，既不知草木之名，亦未達文章之意。

translations.literal: Eggplant is lotus; if lotus replaces water plants, altering antiquity to follow the present, one neither knows the names of plants nor understands the meaning of patterned emblems.
translations.idiomatic: Eggplant is lotus; substituting lotus for water plants alters antiquity to follow the present, showing ignorance both of plant names and of emblematic meaning.

sentences.zh: 此又不經之甚也。

translations.literal: This too is exceedingly unreasonable.
translations.idiomatic: This too is exceedingly unreasonable.

sentences.zh: 又「毳冕六章，三品服之」者。

translations.literal: Again: "Feather miǎn with six patterns, for third rank to wear."
translations.idiomatic: Again: "Feather miǎn with six patterns for third rank."

sentences.zh: 按此王者祀四望服之名也。

translations.literal: Examining this, it is the name of the king's robe for sacrificing to the Four Sacred Peaks.
translations.idiomatic: This is the name of the king's robe for sacrificing to the Four Sacred Peaks.

sentences.zh: 今三品乃得同王之毳冕，而三公不得同王之袞名。

translations.literal: Now third rank would wear the same feather miǎn as the king, yet the Three Dukes may not share the king's dragon robe name.
translations.idiomatic: Third rank would wear the king's feather miǎn, yet the Three Dukes may not share the king's dragon robe name.

sentences.zh: 豈惟顛倒衣裳，抑亦自相矛盾。

translations.literal: Not only are garments inverted— they contradict themselves.
translations.idiomatic: This not only inverts proper dress but contradicts itself.

sentences.zh: 此又不經之甚也。

translations.literal: This too is exceedingly unreasonable.
translations.idiomatic: This too is exceedingly unreasonable.

sentences.zh: 又「黼冕四章，五品服之」。

translations.literal: Again: "Axe miǎn with four patterns, for fifth rank to wear."
translations.idiomatic: Again: "Axe miǎn with four patterns for fifth rank."

sentences.zh: 考之于古，則無其名；

translations.literal: Examining antiquity, there is no such name;
translations.idiomatic: Antiquity knows no such name;

sentences.zh: 驗之於今，則非章首。

translations.literal: testing the present, it is not a leading pattern.
translations.idiomatic: and in present practice it is not a leading pattern.

sentences.zh: 此又不經之甚也。

translations.literal: This too is exceedingly unreasonable.
translations.idiomatic: This too is exceedingly unreasonable.

sentences.zh: 若夫禮惟從俗，則命為制，令為詔，乃秦皇之故事，猶可以適於今矣。

translations.literal: If ritual follows custom alone, then decree as statute and order as edict are Qin precedents and could still suit the present.
translations.idiomatic: If ritual follows custom alone, Qin precedents of decree and edict could still suit the present.

sentences.zh: 若乃義取隨時，則出稱警，入稱蹕，乃漢國之舊儀，猶可以行於代矣。

translations.literal: If meaning follows the times, then proclamation on departure and clearance on entry are Han precedents and could still be practiced in later ages.
translations.idiomatic: If meaning follows the times, Han precedents of proclamation on departure and clearance on entry could still be practiced in later ages.

sentences.zh: 亦何取于變周公之軌物，改宣尼之法度者哉！

translations.literal: Why then take from altering the Duke of Zhou's established standards and changing Confucius's ritual norms!
translations.idiomatic: Why then alter the Duke of Zhou's established standards and Confucius's ritual norms!

sentences.zh: 由是竟寢知機所請。

translations.literal: For this reason Zhiji's request was finally shelved.
translations.idiomatic: For this reason Su Zhiji's request was finally shelved.

sentences.zh: 景龍二年七月，皇太子將親釋奠于國學，有司草儀注，令從臣皆乘馬著衣冠。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the second year of Jinglong, the Crown Prince was to perform the school sacrifice in person at the Directorate; the relevant offices drafted ritual notes ordering accompanying ministers all to ride horses in cap and garments.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of Jinglong 2, as the Crown Prince was to perform the school sacrifice at the Directorate in person, officials drafted ritual notes ordering accompanying ministers to ride horses in full cap and garments.

sentences.zh: 太子左庶子劉子玄進議曰：

translations.literal: Left Vice Director of the Crown Prince's Household Liu Zixuan submitted a memorial stating:
translations.idiomatic: Left Vice Director Liu Zixuan submitted a memorial:

sentences.zh: 古者自大夫已上皆乘車，而以馬為騑服。

translations.literal: In antiquity from grand masters upward all rode in carriages, using horses as outriders.
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity officials from grand master upward rode in carriages, with horses as outriders.

sentences.zh: 魏、晉已降，迄于隋代，朝士又駕牛車，歷代經史，具有其事，不可一二言也。

translations.literal: From Wei and Jin downward through the Sui, court officials again drove ox carts; dynastic histories record this and it cannot be told in a word or two.
translations.idiomatic: From Wei and Jin through Sui, court officials again drove ox carts—a fact abundantly recorded in dynastic histories.

sentences.zh: 至如李廣北征，解鞍憩息；

translations.literal: Consider Li Guang on the northern campaign, removing saddle to rest;
translations.idiomatic: Consider Li Guang on the northern campaign, removing his saddle to rest;

sentences.zh: 馬援南伐，據鞍顧盼。

translations.literal: Ma Yuan on the southern campaign, leaning on saddle and glancing about.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Yuan on the southern campaign, leaning on his saddle and glancing about.

sentences.zh: 斯則鞍馬之設，行於軍旅，戎服所乘，貴于便習者也。

translations.literal: Thus the provision of saddled horses was used in military campaigns; what martial dress rode valued convenience and familiarity.
translations.idiomatic: Saddled horses belonged to the military sphere—the mount of martial dress, valued above all for ease and practical habit.

sentences.zh: 案江左官至尚書郎而輒輕乘馬，則為御史所彈。

translations.literal: According to Jiangzuo precedent, if one reached the rank of Gentleman of the Masters of Writing and casually rode a horse, one would be impeached by the censor.
translations.idiomatic: In the Jiangzuo courts, a man who had risen to Gentleman of the Masters of Writing and then rode a horse lightly or casually would be impeached by the censor.

sentences.zh: 又顏延之罷官後，好騎馬出入閭里，當代稱其放誕。

translations.literal: Also, after Yan Yanzhi was dismissed from office, he liked to ride horses in and out of neighborhoods, and his contemporaries called him unrestrained.
translations.idiomatic: After Yan Yanzhi left office, he took to riding through the lanes of the city, and his contemporaries called him eccentric and unrestrained.

sentences.zh: 此則專車憑軾，右擐朝衣；

translations.literal: In such cases one had a dedicated carriage and leaned on the curb, putting on court robes on the right;
translations.idiomatic: In such cases one rode in a dedicated carriage, leaning on the handrail while donning court robes on the right side;

sentences.zh: 單馬禦鞍，宜從褻服。

translations.literal: Riding a single horse facing the saddle, one should wear informal dress.
translations.idiomatic: when riding a single horse in the saddle, one ought to wear informal dress.

sentences.zh: 求之近古，灼然之明驗矣。

translations.literal: Seeking this in recent antiquity, it is clearly proven evidence.
translations.idiomatic: Look to recent antiquity, and the proof is unmistakable.

sentences.zh: 自皇家撫運，沿革隨時。

translations.literal: Since the imperial house received the mandate, changes followed the times.
translations.idiomatic: Since our dynasty received Heaven's mandate, custom has changed with the times.

sentences.zh: 至如陵廟巡幸，王公冊命，則盛服冠履，乘彼輅車。

translations.literal: As for imperial tomb tours and investiture of princes and dukes, then in full dress with cap and shoes, one rode that imperial carriage.
translations.idiomatic: For tours of imperial tombs and the investiture of princes and dukes, one wore full ceremonial dress with cap and shoes and rode in the imperial carriage.

sentences.zh: 其士庶有衣冠親迎者，亦時以服箱充馭。

translations.literal: For gentlemen and commoners making formal marriage calls in cap and garments, they sometimes used the box carriage as transport.
translations.idiomatic: When gentlemen and commoners went to fetch a bride in formal cap and garments, they sometimes used a box carriage for the journey.

sentences.zh: 在於他事，無復乘車，貴賤所行，通鞍馬而已。

translations.literal: For other matters carriages were no longer used; what nobles and commoners traveled by was universally saddle and horse only.
translations.idiomatic: For all other business, carriages fell out of use; high and low alike traveled by saddle and horse alone.

sentences.zh: 臣伏見比者鑾輿出幸，法駕首途，左右侍臣皆以朝服乘馬。

translations.literal: Your subject humbly observes that recently when the imperial carriage went out on tour and the ceremonial escort set out, the attendant ministers on left and right all rode horses in court dress.
translations.idiomatic: Your subject humbly observes that recently, whenever the imperial carriage set out and the ceremonial escort took the road, the attendant ministers on either side all rode horses in court dress.

sentences.zh: 夫冠履而出，止可配車而行，今乘車即停，而冠履不易，可謂唯知其一而未知其二。

translations.literal: Wearing cap and shoes to go out ought only to be paired with riding in a carriage; now one rides in a carriage and stops, yet cap and shoes are not changed—this may be said to know only one thing and not know the second.
translations.idiomatic: Cap and shoes are meant for going out in a carriage; to ride in a carriage, dismount, and yet leave cap and shoes unchanged is to grasp only half the rule and miss the other half.

sentences.zh: 何者？

translations.literal: Why?
translations.idiomatic: Why is this so?

sentences.zh: 褒衣博帶，革履高冠，本非馬上所施，自是車中之服。

translations.literal: Loose robes and broad sashes, leather shoes and tall caps—these are originally not what is worn on horseback; they are garments of the carriage.
translations.idiomatic: Loose robes and broad sashes, leather shoes and tall caps were never meant for horseback; they are dress for riding in a carriage.

sentences.zh: 必也韈而升鐙，跣以乘鞍，非惟不師古道，亦自取驚今俗，求諸折中，進退無可。

translations.literal: If one must wear socks to mount the stirrup and go barefoot to ride the saddle, this not only fails to follow the ancient way but also startles present custom; seeking a compromise, there is no acceptable course whether advancing or retreating.
translations.idiomatic: If one must wear socks to mount the stirrup yet go barefoot in the saddle, one not only abandons the ancient way but also shocks present custom; seek a middle course, and there is no acceptable path forward or back.

sentences.zh: 且長裙廣袖，襜如翼如，鳴珮紆組，鏘鏘弈弈，馳驟於風塵之內，出入於旌棨之間，儻馬有驚逸，人從顛墜，遂使屬車之右，遺履不收，清道之傍，絓驂相續，固以受嗤行路，有損威儀。

translations.literal: Moreover long skirts and wide sleeves, flowing like wings, tinkling pendants and trailing ribbons, clashing and flashing, galloping within wind and dust, passing in and out among banners and halberds—if the horse should bolt, people fall headlong, so that to the right of the following carriage shoes are left behind unrecovered, beside the cleared road entangled outriders follow one after another—surely this invites mockery from passersby and damages ceremonial dignity.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, long skirts and wide sleeves billow like wings; tinkling pendants and trailing ribbons flash and clash as men gallop through wind and dust, passing among banners and halberds. Should a horse bolt, riders are thrown headlong; shoes are left unrecovered beside the following carriage, and entangled outriders pile up along the cleared road. Such scenes invite the mockery of passersby and diminish ceremonial dignity.

sentences.zh: 今議者皆云秘閣有《梁武南郊圖》，多有衣冠乘馬者，此則近代故事，不得謂無其文。

translations.literal: Now those who debate all say the Secretariat holds a Liang Wu Southern Suburban Sacrifice Picture with many in cap and garments riding horses—this is a recent precedent, and one cannot say there is no written record.
translations.idiomatic: Those who argue the point now say the Secretariat holds a painting of Emperor Wu of Liang's southern suburban sacrifice showing many men in cap and garments on horseback—that is a recent precedent, and one cannot claim there is no textual basis for it.

sentences.zh: 臣案此圖是後人所為，非當時所撰。

translations.literal: Your subject finds this picture was made by later people, not composed at the time.
translations.idiomatic: Your subject finds that this painting was the work of later hands, not something composed in its own day.

sentences.zh: 且觀當今有古今圖畫者多矣，如張僧繇畫《群公祖二疏》，而兵士有著芒屩者；

translations.literal: Moreover, looking at the many ancient and modern paintings today, such as Zhang Sengyou's painting The Officials Bidding Farewell to the Two Shu, in which soldiers wear straw sandals;
translations.idiomatic: Consider how many ancient and modern paintings survive today: in Zhang Sengyou's painting of the officials bidding farewell to the Two Shu, soldiers wear straw sandals;

sentences.zh: 閻立本畫《昭君入匈奴》，而婦人有著帷帽者。

translations.literal: Yan Liben's painting Wang Zhaojun Enters the Xiongnu, in which women wear veiled caps.
translations.idiomatic: in Yan Liben's painting of Wang Zhaojun entering the Xiongnu, women wear veiled caps.

sentences.zh: 夫芒屩出於水鄉，非京華所有；

translations.literal: Straw sandals come from water regions, not found in the capital;
translations.idiomatic: Straw sandals belong to river country, not to the capital;

sentences.zh: 帷帽創于隋代，非漢宮所作。

translations.literal: Veiled caps were created in the Sui, not made in Han palaces.
translations.idiomatic: veiled caps were invented in the Sui, not fashioned in Han palaces.

sentences.zh: 議者豈可征此二畫以為故實者乎！

translations.literal: Can those who debate cite these two paintings as established fact!
translations.idiomatic: Surely those who argue the point cannot cite these two paintings as established historical fact!

sentences.zh: 由斯而言，則《梁武南郊之圖》，義同於此。

translations.literal: From this reasoning, the Liang Wu Southern Suburban Sacrifice Picture is the same in principle.
translations.idiomatic: On this reasoning, the painting of Liang Wu's southern suburban sacrifice stands on the same footing.

sentences.zh: 又傳稱義惟因俗，禮貴緣情。

translations.literal: Also tradition says righteousness adapts to custom, and ritual values following feeling.
translations.idiomatic: Tradition also holds that righteousness follows custom, and ritual honors human feeling.

sentences.zh: 殷輅周冕，規模不一；

translations.literal: Yin chariots and Zhou caps—the models are not uniform;
translations.idiomatic: Yin chariots and Zhou caps did not follow one pattern;

sentences.zh: 秦冠漢珮，用舍無恆。

translations.literal: Qin caps and Han pendants—use and discard are not constant.
translations.idiomatic: Qin caps and Han pendants were adopted and set aside without fixed rule.

sentences.zh: 況我國家道軼百王，功高萬古，事有不便，資於變通。

translations.literal: Moreover our state's Way surpasses the hundred kings, its merit higher than ten thousand ages—when matters are inconvenient, one relies on flexible adaptation.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, our dynasty's Way surpasses the kings of old and its merit towers over ten thousand ages; when a practice proves inconvenient, we may rely on flexible adaptation.

sentences.zh: 其乘馬衣冠，竊謂宜從省廢。

translations.literal: As for riding horses in cap and garments, your subject privately holds it should be simplified and abolished.
translations.idiomatic: As for riding horses in cap and ceremonial garments, your subject respectfully submits that the practice ought to be simplified and abolished.

sentences.zh: 臣此異議，其來自久，日不暇給，未及榷揚。

translations.literal: Your subject's dissent on this has come from long ago; days allowed no leisure, and there was no time to promote it.
translations.idiomatic: Your subject has held this dissent for a long time, but days have allowed no leisure, and there has been no opportunity to press the point.

sentences.zh: 今屬殿下親從齒胄，將臨國學，凡有衣冠乘馬，皆憚此行，所以輒進狂言，用申鄙見。

translations.literal: Now that Your Highness personally follows bearing arms and cap, about to visit the Directorate, all who would ride horses in cap and garments dread this trip—therefore your subject rashly advances wild words to state humble views.
translations.idiomatic: Now that Your Highness is to visit the Directorate in person, bearing arms and cap, all who would ride horses in cap and garments dread the journey. Your subject therefore ventures these rash words to set forth his humble view.

sentences.zh: 皇太子手令付外宣行，仍編入令，以為恆式。

translations.literal: The Crown Prince issued a handwritten order for external promulgation, and it was incorporated into regulations as a permanent rule.
translations.idiomatic: The Crown Prince issued a handwritten order for public promulgation, and it was incorporated into statute as a permanent rule.

sentences.zh: 宴服，蓋古之褻服也，今亦謂之常服。

translations.literal: Banquet dress is essentially the ancient informal dress; today it is also called ordinary dress.
translations.idiomatic: Banquet dress was essentially the ancient informal dress; today it is also called ordinary dress.

sentences.zh: 江南則以巾褐裙襦，北朝則雜以戎夷之制。

translations.literal: In Jiangnan they used headcloth, brown clothes, skirts and short jackets; in the Northern courts they mixed in military and barbarian styles.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiangnan people wore headcloths, brown garments, skirts, and short jackets; in the Northern courts dress mixed in military and barbarian styles.

sentences.zh: 爰至北齊，有長帽短靴，合袴襖子，朱紫玄黃，各任所好。

translations.literal: Reaching Northern Qi, there were long caps, short boots, combined trousers and padded jackets, scarlet, purple, black and yellow—each according to preference.
translations.idiomatic: By Northern Qi there were long caps, short boots, combined trousers and padded jackets in scarlet, purple, black, and yellow, each man dressing as he pleased.

sentences.zh: 雖謁見君上，出入省寺，若非元正大會，一切通用。

translations.literal: Even for audiences with the sovereign and going in and out of ministry halls, unless for New Year's grand assembly, all were universally worn.
translations.idiomatic: Even for audiences with the sovereign and for going in and out of ministry halls, these were worn for all occasions except the New Year's grand assembly.

sentences.zh: 高氏諸帝，常服緋袍。

translations.literal: The Gao emperors commonly wore scarlet robes.
translations.idiomatic: The emperors of the Gao house commonly wore scarlet robes.

sentences.zh: 隋代帝王貴臣，多服黃文綾袍，烏紗帽，九環帶，烏皮六合靴。

translations.literal: Sui imperial nobles and high ministers mostly wore yellow patterned damask robes, black gauze caps, nine-ring belts, and black leather six-panel boots.
translations.idiomatic: In the Sui, emperors and high ministers mostly wore yellow patterned damask robes, black gauze caps, nine-ring belts, and black leather six-panel boots.

sentences.zh: 百官常服，同於匹庶，皆著黃袍，出入殿省。

translations.literal: Officials' ordinary dress was the same as commoners—all wore yellow robes, going in and out of palace halls.
translations.idiomatic: The ordinary dress of officials was the same as that of commoners: all wore yellow robes when entering and leaving the palace halls.

sentences.zh: 天子朝服亦如之，惟帶加十三環以為差異，蓋取於便事。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven's court dress was likewise, only the belt was increased to thirteen rings as distinction—presumably for convenience.
translations.idiomatic: The Son of Heaven's court dress was the same, except that his belt bore thirteen rings as a mark of distinction—presumably for convenience.

sentences.zh: 其烏紗帽漸廢，貴賤通服折上巾，其制周武帝建德年所造也。

translations.literal: The black gauze cap was gradually abandoned; nobles and commoners universally wore the folded-up kerchief, a style created in the Jiande era of Emperor Wu of Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: The black gauze cap gradually fell out of use, and high and low alike wore the folded-up kerchief, a style created in the Jiande era of Emperor Wu of Northern Zhou.

sentences.zh: 晉公宇文護始命袍加下襴。

translations.literal: Duke of Jin Yuwen Hu first ordered robes to have added lower flaps.
translations.idiomatic: The Duke of Jin, Yuwen Hu, first ordered robes to be given added lower flaps.

sentences.zh: 及大業元年，煬帝始制詔吏部尚書牛弘、工部尚書宇文愷、兼內史侍郎虞世基、給事郎許善心、儀曹郎袁朗等憲章古則，創造衣冠，自天子逮于胥吏，章服皆有等差。

translations.literal: In the first year of Daye, Emperor Yang first issued an edict ordering Minister of Personnel Niu Hong, Minister of Works Yuwen Kai, Vice Director of the Secretariat Yu Shiji, Attendant Lang Xu Shanxin, Bureau of Ritual Lang Yuan Lang and others to take ancient rules as law and create caps and garments—from the Son of Heaven down to clerks, regulated dress all had grades.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Daye, Emperor Yang issued an edict ordering Minister of Personnel Niu Hong, Minister of Works Yuwen Kai, Vice Director of the Secretariat Yu Shiji, Attendant Xu Shanxin, Ritual Officer Yuan Lang, and others to take ancient rules as their model and devise caps and garments. From the Son of Heaven down to clerks, regulated dress was graded by rank.

sentences.zh: 始令五品以上，通服朱紫。

translations.literal: At first officials of fifth rank and above universally wore scarlet and purple.
translations.idiomatic: At first officials of fifth rank and above were permitted to wear scarlet and purple.

sentences.zh: 是後師旅務殷，車駕多行幸，百官行從，雖服袴褶，而軍間不便。

translations.literal: After this military affairs were pressing, the imperial carriage often traveled; officials accompanying, though wearing trousers and short coats, found them inconvenient in camp.
translations.idiomatic: After this military affairs grew pressing and the imperial carriage often traveled on tour; officials who accompanied him, though wearing trousers and short coats, found them inconvenient in camp.

sentences.zh: 六年，復詔從駕涉遠者，文武官等皆戎衣，貴賤異等，雜用五色。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, another edict: those accompanying the carriage on distant journeys, civil and military officials all wore martial dress, with noble and common grades distinguished, mixing five colors.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year another edict ordered that civil and military officials accompanying the emperor on distant journeys should all wear martial dress, with grades of nobility and common rank distinguished by a mixture of five colors.

sentences.zh: 五品已上，通著紫袍，六品已下，兼用緋綠。

translations.literal: Fifth rank and above universally wore purple robes; sixth rank and below used scarlet and green together.
translations.idiomatic: Fifth rank and above universally wore purple robes; sixth rank and below wore scarlet and green together.

sentences.zh: 胥吏以青，庶人以白，屠商以皁，士卒以黃。

translations.literal: Clerks in blue, commoners in white, butchers and merchants in black, soldiers in yellow.
translations.idiomatic: Clerks wore blue, commoners white, butchers and merchants black, and soldiers yellow.

sentences.zh: 武德初，因隋舊制，天子宴服，亦名常服，唯以黃袍及衫，後漸用赤黃，遂禁士庶不得以赤黃為衣服雜飾。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Wude, following Sui old regulations, the Son of Heaven's banquet dress, also called ordinary dress, was only yellow robes and tunics; later gradually using red-yellow, then forbidding gentlemen and commoners from using red-yellow for clothing or ornaments.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Wude, following Sui precedent, the Son of Heaven's banquet dress—also called ordinary dress—consisted only of yellow robes and tunics. Later red-yellow came into use, and gentlemen and commoners were forbidden to use red-yellow in clothing or ornaments.

sentences.zh: 四年八月敕：「三品已上，大科紬綾及羅，其色紫，飾用玉。

translations.literal: Fourth year, eighth month edict: Third rank and above, large-grade coarse silk damask and gauze, color purple, ornamented with jade.
translations.idiomatic: An edict of the eighth month of the fourth year read: "Third rank and above shall wear large-grade coarse silk damask and gauze in purple, ornamented with jade.

sentences.zh: 五品已上，小科紬綾及羅，其色朱，飾用金。

translations.literal: Fifth rank and above, small-grade coarse silk damask and gauze, color vermilion, ornamented with gold.
translations.idiomatic: Fifth rank and above shall wear small-grade coarse silk damask and gauze in vermilion, ornamented with gold.

sentences.zh: 六品已上，服絲布，雜小綾，交梭，雙紃，其色黃。

translations.literal: Sixth rank and above, wear silk cloth, mixed small damask, crossed weave, double piping, color yellow.
translations.idiomatic: Sixth rank and above shall wear silk cloth, mixed small damask, crossed weave, and double piping in yellow.

sentences.zh: 六品、七品飾銀。

translations.literal: Sixth and seventh ranks ornamented with silver.
translations.idiomatic: Sixth and seventh ranks shall be ornamented with silver.

sentences.zh: 八品、九品鍮石。

translations.literal: Eighth and ninth ranks, copper-stone.
translations.idiomatic: Eighth and ninth ranks with copper-stone ornaments.

sentences.zh: 流外及庶人服紬、絁、布，其色通用黃。

translations.literal: Those outside the regular ranks and commoners wear coarse silk, silk gauze, and cloth, color universally yellow.
translations.idiomatic: Those outside the regular ranks and commoners shall wear coarse silk, silk gauze, and cloth, universally in yellow.

sentences.zh: 飾用銅鐵。

translations.literal: Ornamented with copper and iron.
translations.idiomatic: Their ornaments shall be of copper and iron.

sentences.zh: 」五品已上執象笏。

translations.literal: Fifth rank and above hold ivory tablets.
translations.idiomatic: Fifth rank and above shall carry ivory tablets.

sentences.zh: 三品已下前挫後直，五品已上前挫後屈。

translations.literal: Third rank and below, front beveled and rear straight; fifth rank and above, front beveled and rear bent.
translations.idiomatic: For third rank and below the front was beveled and the rear straight; for fifth rank and above the front was beveled and the rear curved.

sentences.zh: 自有唐已來，一例上圓下方，曾不分別。

translations.literal: Since Tang began, uniformly round above and square below, never distinguished.
translations.idiomatic: Since the Tang began, all tablets were uniformly round above and square below, with no distinction by rank.

sentences.zh: 六品已下，執竹木為笏，上挫下方。

translations.literal: Sixth rank and below hold bamboo and wood as tablets, upper beveled and lower square.
translations.idiomatic: Sixth rank and below carried tablets of bamboo or wood, beveled above and square below.

sentences.zh: 其折上巾，烏皮六合靴，貴賤通用。

translations.literal: The folded-up kerchief and black leather six-panel boots were universally worn by nobles and commoners.
translations.idiomatic: The folded-up kerchief and black leather six-panel boots were worn alike by high and low.

sentences.zh: 貞觀四年又制，三品已上服紫，五品已下服緋，六品、七品服綠，八品、九品服以青，帶以鍮石。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Zhenguan another regulation: third rank and above wear purple, fifth rank and below wear scarlet, sixth and seventh ranks wear green, eighth and ninth ranks wear blue, belts of copper-stone.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Zhenguan another regulation was issued: third rank and above wore purple; fifth rank and below wore scarlet; sixth and seventh ranks wore green; eighth and ninth ranks wore blue; belts were of copper-stone.

sentences.zh: 婦人從夫色。

translations.literal: Women follow their husbands' colors.
translations.idiomatic: Women followed their husbands' colors.

sentences.zh: 雖有令，仍許通著黃。

translations.literal: Although there was an order, yellow was still permitted to be worn universally.
translations.idiomatic: Despite the regulation, yellow dress was still permitted generally.

sentences.zh: 五年八月敕，七品已上，服龜甲雙巨十花綾，其色綠。

translations.literal: Fifth year, eighth month edict: seventh rank and above wear tortoise-shell double-giant ten-flower damask, color green.
translations.idiomatic: An edict of the eighth month of the fifth year ordered seventh rank and above to wear tortoise-shell double-giant ten-flower damask in green.

sentences.zh: 九品已上，服絲布及雜小綾，其色青。

translations.literal: Ninth rank and above wear silk cloth and mixed small damask, color blue.
translations.idiomatic: Ninth rank and above wore silk cloth and mixed small damask in blue.

sentences.zh: 十一月，賜諸衛將軍紫袍，錦為褾袖。

translations.literal: Eleventh month, bestowed on the guard generals purple robes, brocade for collar and sleeves.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month purple robes were bestowed on the guard generals, with brocade at collar and sleeves.

sentences.zh: 八年五月，太宗初服翼善冠，貴臣服進德冠。

translations.literal: Eighth year, fifth month, Taizong first wore the Yishan cap; nobles wore the Jinde cap.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the eighth year, Emperor Taizong first wore the Yishan cap, and nobles wore the Jinde cap.

sentences.zh: 龍朔二年，司禮少常伯孫茂道奏稱：「舊令六品、七品著綠，八品、九品著青，深青亂紫，非卑品所服。

translations.literal: Second year of Longshuo, Vice Director of the Ministry of Rites Sun Maodao submitted a memorial stating: The old order had sixth and seventh ranks wear green, eighth and ninth ranks wear blue; deep blue confuses with purple and is not what low ranks should wear.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Longshuo, Vice Director of the Ministry of Rites Sun Maodao submitted a memorial: "Under the old regulation sixth and seventh ranks wore green and eighth and ninth ranks wore blue. Deep blue is too close to purple and is not fitting dress for the lower ranks.

sentences.zh: 望請改八品、九品著碧。

translations.literal: I respectfully request changing eighth and ninth ranks to wear jade-green.
translations.idiomatic: I respectfully request that eighth and ninth ranks be changed to jade-green.

sentences.zh: 朝參之處，聽兼服黃。

translations.literal: At court attendance, permission is granted to wear yellow as well.
translations.idiomatic: At court attendance they may also wear yellow.

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: The request was granted.
translations.idiomatic: The request was granted.

sentences.zh: 總章元年，始一切不許著黃。

translations.literal: First year of Zongzhang, yellow dress was altogether forbidden.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Zongzhang, yellow dress was altogether forbidden.

sentences.zh: 上元元年八月又制：「一品已下帶手巾、算袋，仍佩刀子、礪石，武官欲帶者聽之。

translations.literal: First year of Shangyuan, eighth month, another regulation: First rank and below carry hand towels and abacus bags, and still wear knives and whetstones; military officers who wish to carry them are permitted.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of the first year of Shangyuan another regulation was issued: "First rank and below shall carry hand towels and abacus bags, and shall also wear knives and whetstones; military officers who wish to carry them are permitted to do so.

sentences.zh: 文武三品已上服紫，金玉帶。

translations.literal: Civil and military third rank and above wear purple, jade and gold belts.
translations.idiomatic: Civil and military officials of third rank and above wore purple with jade and gold belts.

sentences.zh: 四品服深緋，五品服淺緋，並金帶。

translations.literal: Fourth rank wears deep scarlet, fifth rank wears light scarlet, all with gold belts.
translations.idiomatic: Fourth rank wore deep scarlet and fifth rank light scarlet, both with gold belts.

sentences.zh: 六品服深綠，七品服淺綠，並銀帶。

translations.literal: Sixth rank wears deep green, seventh rank wears light green, all with silver belts.
translations.idiomatic: Sixth rank wore deep green and seventh rank light green, both with silver belts.

sentences.zh: 八品服深青，九品服淺青，並鍮石帶。

translations.literal: Eighth rank wears deep blue, ninth rank wears light blue, all with copper-stone belts.
translations.idiomatic: Eighth rank wore deep blue and ninth rank light blue, both with copper-stone belts.

sentences.zh: 庶人並銅鐵帶。

translations.literal: Commoners all copper and iron belts.
translations.idiomatic: Commoners all wore copper and iron belts.

sentences.zh: 」文明元年七月甲寅詔：「旗幟皆從金色，飾之以紫，畫以雜文。

translations.literal: First year of Wenming, seventh month, day jiayin edict: Banners and flags all follow golden color, ornamented with purple, painted with mixed patterns.
translations.idiomatic: An edict of the day jiayin in the seventh month of the first year of Wenming read: "Banners and flags shall all follow golden color, ornamented with purple and painted with mixed patterns.

sentences.zh: 八品已下舊服者，並改以碧。

translations.literal: Eighth rank and below who formerly wore blue, all changed to jade-green.
translations.idiomatic: Those of eighth rank and below who had formerly worn blue were all changed to jade-green.

sentences.zh: 京文官五品已上，六品已下，七品清官，每日入朝，常服袴褶。

translations.literal: Capital civil officials fifth rank and above, sixth rank and below, seventh-rank pure officials, entering court daily, ordinarily wear trousers and short coats.
translations.idiomatic: Capital civil officials of fifth rank and above, sixth rank and below, and seventh-rank pure officials entering court daily wore trousers and short coats as ordinary dress.

sentences.zh: 諸州縣長官在公衙，亦准此。

translations.literal: Prefectural and county chiefs in public offices likewise follow this.
translations.idiomatic: Prefectural and county chiefs in their public offices followed the same rule.

sentences.zh: 」景雲中又制，令依上元故事，一品已下帶手巾、算袋，其刀子、礪石等許不佩。

translations.literal: In Jingyun another regulation again ordered following Shangyuan precedent: first rank and below carry hand towels and abacus bags; knives, whetstones and the like are permitted not to be worn.
translations.idiomatic: In Jingyun another regulation ordered that, following Shangyuan precedent, first rank and below should carry hand towels and abacus bags, while knives, whetstones, and the like need not be worn.

sentences.zh: 武官五品已上佩䪓韘七事。

translations.literal: Military officers fifth rank and above wear the seven accoutrements of bow case and archer's thumb ring.
translations.idiomatic: Military officers of fifth rank and above wore the seven accoutrements of bow case and archer's thumb ring.

sentences.zh: 七謂佩刀、刀子、礪石、契苾真、噦厥、針筒、火石袋等也。

translations.literal: The seven means wearing sword, knife, whetstone, qibi zhen, yuejue, needle case, fire-stone pouch, and the like.
translations.idiomatic: The seven items were the sword, knife, whetstone, qibi zhen, yuejue, needle case, and fire-stone pouch.

sentences.zh: 至開元初復罷之。

translations.literal: By the beginning of Kaiyuan it was again abolished.
translations.idiomatic: By the beginning of Kaiyuan the requirement was abolished again.

sentences.zh: 則天天授二年二月，朝集使刺史賜繡袍，各於背上繡成八字銘。

translations.literal: Second year of Tianshou under Empress Zetian, second month, assembly envoys and prefects were bestowed embroidered robes, each with an eight-character inscription embroidered on the back.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the second year of Tianshou under Empress Zetian, assembly envoys and prefects were granted embroidered robes, each bearing an eight-character inscription embroidered on the back.

sentences.zh: 長壽三年四月，敕賜岳牧金字銀字銘袍。

translations.literal: Third year of Changshou, fourth month, an edict bestowed on frontier governors robes inscribed in gold and silver characters.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the third year of Changshou an edict bestowed on frontier governors robes inscribed in gold and silver characters.

sentences.zh: 延載元年五月，則天內出緋紫單羅銘襟背衫，賜文武三品已上。

translations.literal: First year of Yanzai, fifth month, Zetian issued from within scarlet and purple single-gauze inscribed-collar-and-back tunics, bestowed on civil and military third rank and above.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the first year of Yanzai, Empress Zetian issued from the palace scarlet and purple single-gauze tunics with inscribed collar and back, bestowing them on civil and military officials of third rank and above.

sentences.zh: 左右監門衛將軍等飾以對師子，左右衛飾以麒麟，左右武威衛飾以對虎，左右豹韜衛飾以豹，左右鷹揚衛飾以鷹，左右玉鈐衛飾以對鶻，左右金吾衛飾以對豸，諸王飾以盤龍及鹿，宰相飾以鳳池，尚書飾以對雁。

translations.literal: Left and Right Gate Guard generals and the like ornamented with paired lions; Left and Right Guard with qilin; Left and Right Martial Might Guard with paired tigers; Left and Right Leopard Bow Guard with leopards; Left and Right Eagle Banner Guard with eagles; Left and Right Jade Seal Guard with paired falcons; Left and Right Golden Guard with paired zhi; princes with coiled dragons and deer; chancellors with phoenix pool; Masters of Writing with paired geese.
translations.idiomatic: Generals of the Left and Right Gate Guards were ornamented with paired lions; the Left and Right Guards with qilin; the Left and Right Martial Might Guards with paired tigers; the Left and Right Leopard Bow Guards with leopards; the Left and Right Eagle Banner Guards with eagles; the Left and Right Jade Seal Guards with paired falcons; the Left and Right Golden Guards with paired zhi; princes with coiled dragons and deer; chancellors with phoenix pool; and Masters of Writing with paired geese.

sentences.zh: 武德已來，始有巾子，文官名流，上平頭小樣者。

translations.literal: Since Wude there began to be kerchiefs; among civil officials of renown, those of the flat-top small pattern.
translations.idiomatic: Since Wude kerchiefs had appeared; among civil officials of note, the flat-top small style was favored.

sentences.zh: 則天朝，貴臣內賜高頭巾子，呼為武家諸王樣。

translations.literal: In the reign of Zetian, high ministers were granted from within high-crowned kerchiefs, called the style of the Wu princes.
translations.idiomatic: In Empress Zetian's reign high ministers were granted from within high-crowned kerchiefs, called the style of the Wu princes.

sentences.zh: 中宗景龍四年三月，因內宴賜宰臣已下內樣巾子。

translations.literal: Third month of the fourth year of Jinglong under Emperor Zhongzong, on the occasion of an inner banquet, kerchiefs of the inner pattern were bestowed on chancellors and below.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the fourth year of Jinglong under Emperor Zhongzong, at an inner banquet kerchiefs of the palace pattern were bestowed on chancellors and those below them.

sentences.zh: 開元已來，文官士伍多以紫皁官絁為頭巾、平頭巾子，相效為雅制。

translations.literal: Since Kaiyuan, civil officials and gentlemen mostly used purple and black official silk gauze for headcloths and flat-top kerchiefs, emulating one another as refined style.
translations.idiomatic: Since Kaiyuan civil officials and gentlemen had largely taken to purple and black official silk gauze for headcloths and flat-top kerchiefs, emulating one another as refined fashion.

sentences.zh: 玄宗開元十九年十月，賜供奉官及諸司長官羅頭巾及官樣巾子，迄今服之也。

translations.literal: Tenth month of the nineteenth year of Kaiyuan under Emperor Xuanzong, gauze headcloths and official-pattern kerchiefs were bestowed on palace attendants and bureau chiefs; to the present they are worn.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of the nineteenth year of Kaiyuan, Emperor Xuanzong bestowed gauze headcloths and official-pattern kerchiefs on palace attendants and bureau chiefs, and these are still worn today.

sentences.zh: 天寶十載五月，改諸衛旗幡隊仗，先用緋色，並用赤黃色，以符土德。

translations.literal: Fifth month of the tenth year of Tianbao, changed the guard banners, flags, ranks and accoutrements, first using scarlet, all using red-yellow, to accord with the virtue of earth.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the tenth year of Tianbao the banners, flags, ranks, and accoutrements of the guards were changed, scarlet being used first and red-yellow throughout, in accord with the virtue of earth.

sentences.zh: 高祖武德元年九月，改銀菟符為銀魚符。

translations.literal: Ninth month of the first year of Wude under Gaozu, changed the silver hare tally to the silver fish tally.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of the first year of Wude, Emperor Gaozu changed the silver hare tally to the silver fish tally.

sentences.zh: 高宗永徽二年五月，開府儀同三司及京官文武職事四品、五品，並給隨身魚。

translations.literal: Fifth month of the second year of Yonghui under Emperor Gaozong, Grand Preceptor of the State and capital civil and military officeholders of fourth and fifth ranks were all given personal fish tallies.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the second year of Yonghui, Emperor Gaozong granted personal fish tallies to Grand Preceptors of the State and to capital civil and military officeholders of fourth and fifth rank.

sentences.zh: 咸亨三年五月，五品已上賜新魚袋，並飾以銀。

translations.literal: Fifth month of the third year of Xianheng, fifth rank and above were bestowed new fish pouches, all ornamented with silver.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the third year of Xianheng, officials of fifth rank and above were granted new fish pouches, all ornamented with silver.

sentences.zh: 三品已上各賜金裝刀子、礪石一具。

translations.literal: Third rank and above were each bestowed gold-mounted knives and one set of whetstones.
translations.idiomatic: Officials of third rank and above were each granted gold-mounted knives and a set of whetstones.

sentences.zh: 垂拱二年正月，諸州都督刺史，並准京官帶魚袋。

translations.literal: First month of the second year of Chuigong, military governors and prefects of all prefectures were all permitted to wear fish pouches as capital officials did.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the second year of Chuigong, military governors and prefects throughout the provinces were permitted to wear fish pouches on the same terms as capital officials.

sentences.zh: 天授元年九月，改內外所佩魚並作龜。

translations.literal: Ninth month of the first year of Tianshou, changed all fish tallies worn inside and outside the court to tortoise form.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of the first year of Tianshou, all fish tallies worn by officials within and outside the court were changed to tortoise form.

sentences.zh: 久視元年十月，職事三品已上龜袋，宜用金飾，四品用銀飾，五品用銅飾。

translations.literal: Tenth month of the first year of Jiushi, tortoise pouches for active-duty third rank and above should use gold ornament, fourth rank silver ornament, fifth rank bronze ornament.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of the first year of Jiushi, tortoise pouches for active-duty officials of third rank and above were to be ornamented with gold, those of fourth rank with silver, and those of fifth rank with bronze.

sentences.zh: 上守下行，皆從官給。

translations.literal: Upper, shou, lower, and travel grades were all supplied by the office.
translations.idiomatic: The upper, shou, lower, and travel grades of tortoise tally were all supplied by the government.

sentences.zh: 神龍元年二月，內外官五品已上依舊佩魚袋。

translations.literal: Second month of the first year of Shelong, inside and outside officials fifth rank and above again wore fish pouches as before.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the first year of Shelong, officials within and outside the court of fifth rank and above resumed wearing fish pouches as before.

sentences.zh: 六月，郡王、嗣王特許佩金魚袋。

translations.literal: Sixth month, commandery princes and heir princes were specially permitted to wear gold fish pouches.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, commandery princes and heir princes were specially permitted to wear gold fish pouches.

sentences.zh: 景龍三年八月，令特進佩魚。

translations.literal: Eighth month of the third year of Jinglong, ordered that honorary grand mentors wear fish tallies.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of the third year of Jinglong, honorary grand mentors were ordered to wear fish tallies.

sentences.zh: 散職佩魚，自此始也。

translations.literal: Honorary officeholders wearing fish tallies began from this time.
translations.idiomatic: The practice of honorary officeholders wearing fish tallies began at this time.

sentences.zh: 自武德已來，皆正員帶闕官始佩魚袋，員外、判試、檢校自則天、中宗後始有之，皆不佩魚。

translations.literal: Since Wude, only regular appointees holding substantive posts wore fish pouches; supernumerary, acting, probationary, and supervisory appointees appeared only after Zetian and Zhongzong, and none wore fish.
translations.idiomatic: Since Wude only regular appointees holding substantive posts had worn fish pouches; supernumerary, acting, probationary, and supervisory appointees appeared only after Empress Zetian and Emperor Zhongzong, and none of them wore fish tallies.

sentences.zh: 雖正員官得佩，亦去任及致仕即解去魚袋。

translations.literal: Even though regular appointees were permitted to wear them, upon leaving office or retiring they immediately removed their fish pouches.
translations.idiomatic: Even regular appointees permitted to wear fish pouches had to remove them as soon as they left office or retired.

sentences.zh: 至開元九年，張嘉貞為中書令，奏諸致仕許終身佩魚，以為榮寵。

translations.literal: By the ninth year of Kaiyuan, Zhang Jiazhen as Director of the Secretariat memorialized that retired officials be permitted to wear fish tallies for life as an honor.
translations.idiomatic: By the ninth year of Kaiyuan, Zhang Jiazhen, serving as Director of the Secretariat, memorialized that retired officials be permitted to wear fish tallies for life as a mark of honor.

sentences.zh: 以理去任，亦聽佩魚袋。

translations.literal: Those leaving office on proper grounds were also allowed to wear fish pouches.
translations.idiomatic: Those who left office on proper grounds were also permitted to keep wearing fish pouches.

sentences.zh: 自後恩制賜賞緋紫，例兼魚袋，謂之章服，因之佩魚袋、服朱紫者眾矣。

translations.literal: Afterward imperial grace decrees bestowing scarlet and purple rewards routinely included fish pouches, called insignia dress; hence many wore fish pouches and scarlet and purple robes.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter imperial grace decrees granting scarlet and purple rewards routinely included fish pouches as well, a combination called insignia dress; as a result, many more people wore fish pouches and scarlet or purple robes.

sentences.zh: 梁制雲，袴褶，近代服以從戎，今纘嚴則文武百官咸服之。

translations.literal: According to Liang regulations: kuzhe. In recent times the dress was worn for military service; now at solemn assembly rites civil and military officials all wear it.
translations.idiomatic: According to Liang regulations, kuzhe was military dress; in recent times it had been worn for campaigning, but now at solemn assembly rites civil and military officials all wore it.

sentences.zh: 車駕親戎，則縛袴不舒散也。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage personally went to war, the trousers were bound and not left loose.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor personally went to war, the trousers were tied fast and not left hanging loose.

sentences.zh: 中官紫褶，外官絳褶，舄用皮。

translations.literal: Inner officials wore purple kuzhe, outer officials scarlet kuzhe, and shoes were of leather.
translations.idiomatic: Palace officials wore purple kuzhe, outside officials scarlet kuzhe, and shoes were made of leather.

sentences.zh: 服冠衣朱者，紫衣用赤舄，烏衣用烏舄。

translations.literal: Those wearing caps and vermilion dress used red shoes with purple robes and black shoes with black robes.
translations.idiomatic: Those wearing caps and vermilion dress wore red shoes with purple robes and black shoes with black robes.

sentences.zh: 唯褶服以靴。

translations.literal: Only kuzhe dress used boots.
translations.idiomatic: Only kuzhe dress was worn with boots.

sentences.zh: 靴，胡履也，取便於事，施於戎服。

translations.literal: Boots were foreign shoes, taken for convenience in action, and applied to military dress.
translations.idiomatic: Boots were foreign footwear, chosen for convenience in action and adopted for military dress.

sentences.zh: 舊制，乘輿案褥、床褥、床帷，皆以紫為飾。

translations.literal: Under the old regulations, the imperial carriage cushions, bed cushions, and bed curtains all used purple as ornament.
translations.idiomatic: Under the old regulations, the cushions and curtains of the imperial carriage, bed, and couch were all ornamented in purple.

sentences.zh: 天寶六載，禮儀使太常卿韋糸舀奏請依禦袍色，以赤黃為飾。

translations.literal: Sixth year of Tianbao, Director of Ceremonies Grand Minister of Ceremonies Wei Tao memorialized requesting that ornament follow the color of the imperial robe, using red-yellow as ornament.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Tianbao, Wei Tao, serving as Director of Ceremonies and Grand Minister of Ceremonies, memorialized that the ornamentation follow the color of the imperial robe and use red-yellow instead.

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: The request was approved.
translations.idiomatic: The request was approved.

sentences.zh: 《武德令》：皇后服有褘衣、鞠衣、鈿釵禮衣三等。

translations.literal: Wude Code: the empress's dress included three grades—huiyi, juyi, and dianchai liyi.
translations.idiomatic: The Wude Code prescribed three grades of empress's dress: huiyi, juyi, and dianchai liyi.

sentences.zh: 褘衣，首飾花十二樹，並兩博鬢，其衣以深青織成為之，文為翬翟之形。

translations.literal: Huiyi: head ornament of twelve tree-flowers, together with two broad side locks; the robe was woven in deep blue-green, patterned in the form of hui pheasants.
translations.idiomatic: Huiyi had a head ornament of twelve tree-flowers and two broad side locks; the robe was woven in deep blue-green with patterns of hui pheasants.

sentences.zh: 素紗中單，黼領，羅縠褾、襈，蔽膝，大帶，以青衣，革帶，青韈、舄，白玉雙珮，玄組雙大綬。

translations.literal: Plain gauze inner robe, fu collar, silk gauze cuffs and border, knee cover, great belt, green outer robe, leather belt, green socks and shoes, paired white jade pendants, and paired black-cord great sashes.
translations.idiomatic: It was worn with a plain gauze inner robe, fu collar, silk gauze cuffs and border, knee cover, great belt, green outer robe, leather belt, green socks and shoes, paired white jade pendants, and paired black-cord great sashes.

sentences.zh: 受冊、助祭、朝會諸大事則服之。

translations.literal: It was worn for receiving the investiture, assisting at sacrifice, court assemblies, and other great occasions.
translations.idiomatic: It was worn for investiture, assisting at sacrifice, court assemblies, and other major state occasions.

sentences.zh: 鞠衣，親蠶則服之。

translations.literal: Juyi was worn when personally supervising the silkworms.
translations.idiomatic: Juyi was worn when the empress personally supervised the silkworms.

sentences.zh: 鈿釵禮衣，十二鈿，服通用雜色，制與上同，唯無雉及珮綬，宴見賓客則服之。

translations.literal: Dianchai liyi had twelve dian ornaments; the dress generally used mixed colors, the design being the same as above except without pheasant emblem and pendant sash; it was worn when banqueting and receiving guests.
translations.idiomatic: Dianchai liyi had twelve dian ornaments and was generally made in mixed colors; its design matched the above except that it lacked pheasant emblem and pendant sash, and it was worn when banqueting and receiving guests.

sentences.zh: 皇太子妃服，首飾花九樹，褕翟。

translations.literal: The crown prince's consort's dress had a head ornament of nine tree-flowers and yu pheasants.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince's consort wore a head ornament of nine tree-flowers and a robe patterned with yu pheasants.

sentences.zh: 素紗中單，黼領，羅縠褾、襈，蔽膝，大帶，以青衣，革帶，青韈、舄，瑜玉珮，紅朱雙大綬。

translations.literal: Plain gauze inner robe, fu collar, silk gauze cuffs and border, knee cover, great belt, green outer robe, leather belt, green socks and shoes, yu jade pendant, and paired scarlet great sashes.
translations.idiomatic: She also wore a plain gauze inner robe, fu collar, silk gauze cuffs and border, knee cover, great belt, green outer robe, leather belt, green socks and shoes, a yu jade pendant, and paired scarlet great sashes.

sentences.zh: 受冊、助祭、朝會諸大事則服之。

translations.literal: It was worn for receiving the investiture, assisting at sacrifice, court assemblies, and other great occasions.
translations.idiomatic: It was worn for investiture, assisting at sacrifice, court assemblies, and other major state occasions.

sentences.zh: 鞠衣，從蠶則服之。

translations.literal: Juyi was worn when accompanying the silkworm rite.
translations.idiomatic: Juyi was worn when accompanying the silkworm rite.

sentences.zh: 鈿釵禮衣，九鈿，服通用雜色，制與上同，唯無雉及珮、綬，宴見賓客則服之。

translations.literal: Dianchai liyi had nine dian ornaments; the dress generally used mixed colors, the design being the same as above except without pheasant emblem and pendant and sash; it was worn when banqueting and receiving guests.
translations.idiomatic: Dianchai liyi had nine dian ornaments and was generally made in mixed colors; its design matched the above except that it lacked pheasant emblem, pendant, and sash, and it was worn when banqueting and receiving guests.

sentences.zh: 內外命婦服花釵，翟衣青質，第一品花鈿九樹，翟九等。

translations.literal: Inside and outside titled ladies wore flowered hairpins; di robes were blue-green in substance. First rank had nine tree-flowers and nine grades of di.
translations.idiomatic: Titled ladies inside and outside the court wore flowered hairpins and blue-green di robes; first rank had nine tree-flowers and nine grades of di pattern.

sentences.zh: 第二品花鈿八樹，翟八等。

translations.literal: Second rank had eight tree-flowers and eight grades of di.
translations.idiomatic: Second rank had eight tree-flowers and eight grades of di pattern.

sentences.zh: 第三品花鈿七樹，翟七等。

translations.literal: Third rank had seven tree-flowers and seven grades of di.
translations.idiomatic: Third rank had seven tree-flowers and seven grades of di pattern.

sentences.zh: 第四品花鈿六樹，翟六等。

translations.literal: Fourth rank had six tree-flowers and six grades of di.
translations.idiomatic: Fourth rank had six tree-flowers and six grades of di pattern.

sentences.zh: 第五品花鈿五樹，翟五等。

translations.literal: Fifth rank had five tree-flowers and five grades of di.
translations.idiomatic: Fifth rank had five tree-flowers and five grades of di pattern.

sentences.zh: 並素紗中單，黼領，朱褾、襈亦通用羅縠也。

translations.literal: All had plain gauze inner robes and fu collars; vermilion cuffs and borders also generally used silk gauze.
translations.idiomatic: All wore plain gauze inner robes and fu collars; vermilion cuffs and borders were also generally made of silk gauze.

sentences.zh: 蔽膝，隨裳色，以緅為領緣，加以文繡，重雉為章二事，一品已下皆同也。

translations.literal: The knee cover followed the color of the skirt, used dark red for collar and border, added patterned embroidery, and had paired pheasants as two emblems; from first rank down all were the same.
translations.idiomatic: The knee cover matched the color of the skirt, with dark red collar and border, patterned embroidery, and paired pheasants as two emblems; from first rank down the rule was the same.

sentences.zh: 大帶，隨衣色，緋其外，上以朱錦，下以綠錦，紐同青組。

translations.literal: The great belt followed the color of the robe, scarlet on the outside, vermilion brocade above and green brocade below, with fasteners like green cord.
translations.idiomatic: The great belt matched the color of the robe, scarlet on the outside, with vermilion brocade above and green brocade below, and fasteners of green cord.

sentences.zh: 青衣，革帶，青韈、舄，珮，綬。

translations.literal: Green outer robe, leather belt, green socks and shoes, pendant, and sash.
translations.idiomatic: They also wore green outer robes, leather belts, green socks and shoes, pendants, and sashes.

sentences.zh: 內命婦受冊、從蠶、朝會則服之；

translations.literal: Inside titled ladies wore it when receiving investiture, accompanying the silkworm rite, and at court assemblies.
translations.idiomatic: Inside titled ladies wore it for investiture, the silkworm rite, and court assemblies;

sentences.zh: 其外命婦嫁及受冊、從蠶、大朝會亦准此。

translations.literal: Outside titled ladies at marriage and when receiving investiture, accompanying the silkworm rite, and at great court assemblies also followed this.
translations.idiomatic: Outside titled ladies also followed this rule at marriage, investiture, the silkworm rite, and great court assemblies.

sentences.zh: 鈿釵禮衣，通用雜色，制與上同，唯無雉及珮綬。

translations.literal: Dianchai liyi generally used mixed colors, the design being the same as above except without pheasant emblem and pendant sash.
translations.idiomatic: Dianchai liyi was generally made in mixed colors; its design matched the above except that it lacked pheasant emblem and pendant sash.

sentences.zh: 去舄，加履。

translations.literal: Shoes were removed and slippers added.
translations.idiomatic: Shoes were removed and replaced with slippers.

sentences.zh: 第一品九鈿，第二品八鈿，第三品七鈿，第四品六鈿，第五品五鈿。

translations.literal: First rank had nine dian, second rank eight dian, third rank seven dian, fourth rank six dian, fifth rank five dian.
translations.idiomatic: First rank had nine dian ornaments, second rank eight, third rank seven, fourth rank six, and fifth rank five.

sentences.zh: 內命婦尋常參見，外命婦朝參辭見及禮會則服之。

translations.literal: Inside titled ladies wore it for ordinary audiences; outside titled ladies wore it for court attendance, farewell audiences, and ceremonial gatherings.
translations.idiomatic: Inside titled ladies wore it for ordinary audiences; outside titled ladies wore it for court attendance, farewell audiences, and ceremonial gatherings.

sentences.zh: 六尚、寶林、御女、采女、女官等服，禮衣通用雜色，制與上同，惟無首飾。

translations.literal: The dress of the Six Bureaus, Treasure Grove, palace women, selected women, and female officials generally used mixed colors for ceremonial dress, the design being the same as above except without head ornaments.
translations.idiomatic: The ceremonial dress of the Six Bureaus, Treasure Grove attendants, palace women, selected women, and female officials was generally made in mixed colors; its design matched the above except that it had no head ornaments.

sentences.zh: 七品已上，有大事服之，尋常供奉則公服。

translations.literal: Seventh rank and above wore it for great occasions; for ordinary palace service they wore official dress.
translations.idiomatic: Those of seventh rank and above wore it for major occasions; for ordinary palace service they wore official dress.

sentences.zh: 公服去中單、蔽膝、大帶。

translations.literal: Official dress omitted the inner robe, knee cover, and great belt.
translations.idiomatic: Official dress omitted the inner robe, knee cover, and great belt.

sentences.zh: 九品已上，大事及尋常供奉，並公服。

translations.literal: Ninth rank and above wore official dress for both great occasions and ordinary palace service.
translations.idiomatic: Those of ninth rank and above wore official dress for both major occasions and ordinary palace service.

sentences.zh: 東宮准此。

translations.literal: The Eastern Palace followed this.
translations.idiomatic: The Eastern Palace followed the same rule.

sentences.zh: 女史則半袖裙襦。

translations.literal: Female clerks wore half-sleeved skirt and jacket.
translations.idiomatic: Female clerks wore half-sleeved skirts and jackets.

sentences.zh: 諸公主、王妃珮綬同，諸王縣主、內命婦准品。

translations.literal: All princesses and prince's consorts had the same pendant and sash; county princesses of princes and inside titled ladies followed rank.
translations.idiomatic: All princesses and princes' consorts wore the same pendants and sashes; county princesses of princes and inside titled ladies followed their respective ranks.

sentences.zh: 外命婦五品已上，皆准夫、子，即非因夫、子別加邑號者，亦准品。

translations.literal: Outside titled ladies of fifth rank and above all followed husband or son; even those granted separate fief titles not through husband or son also followed rank.
translations.idiomatic: Outside titled ladies of fifth rank and above all followed the rank of their husband or son; even those granted separate fief titles not through husband or son also followed their rank.

sentences.zh: 婦人宴服，准令各依夫色，上得兼下，下不得僭上。

translations.literal: Women's banquet dress, according to the code, each followed her husband's color; higher ranks could include lower, but lower could not usurp higher.
translations.idiomatic: Women's banquet dress was regulated by code according to their husbands' colors: higher ranks could include lower ones, but lower ranks could not usurp higher ones.

sentences.zh: 既不在公庭，而風俗奢靡，不依格令，綺羅錦繡，隨所好尚。

translations.literal: Since they were not in the public court, custom grew extravagant and did not follow the regulations; brocades and embroidery followed whatever was favored.
translations.idiomatic: Outside the public court, however, custom grew extravagant and paid little heed to the regulations; brocades and embroidery followed whatever fashion people favored.

sentences.zh: 上自宮掖，下至匹庶，遞相仿效，貴賤無別。

translations.literal: From the palace quarters above down to commoners below, people imitated one another in turn, and noble and base were undifferentiated.
translations.idiomatic: From the palace quarters down to commoners, people copied one another in turn until noble and common were scarcely distinguishable.

sentences.zh: 武德、貞觀之時，宮人騎馬者，依齊、隋舊制，多著羃䍦，雖發自戎夷，而全身障蔽，不欲途路窺之。

translations.literal: In the Wude and Zhenguan periods, palace women who rode horses, following the old Qi and Sui system, mostly wore mili veils; though the custom arose among frontier peoples, it covered the whole body because one did not wish passersby on the road to gaze upon them.
translations.idiomatic: During Wude and Zhenguan, palace women who rode horses mostly wore mili veils, following the old Qi and Sui custom; though the practice came from frontier peoples, it covered the whole body so that passersby on the road could not gaze upon them.

sentences.zh: 王公之家，亦同此制。

translations.literal: Princely and ducal households also followed this regulation.
translations.idiomatic: Princely and ducal households followed the same practice.

sentences.zh: 永徽之後，皆用帷帽，拖裙到頸，漸為淺露。

translations.literal: After Yonghui, all used weimao hats, with trailing skirts reaching the neck, gradually becoming more lightly exposed.
translations.idiomatic: After Yonghui everyone used weimao hats, with trailing skirts reaching the neck, and dress gradually became more revealing.

sentences.zh: 尋下敕禁斷，初雖暫息，旋又仍舊，咸亨二年又下敕曰：「百官家口，咸預士流，至於衢路之間，豈可全無障蔽。

translations.literal: Soon an edict was issued forbidding it; at first the practice briefly ceased, but then it resumed as before. In the second year of Xianheng another edict was issued saying: "The households of officials all belong to the gentry; on public roads, how can there be no screening at all?
translations.idiomatic: An edict was soon issued forbidding the practice; it briefly ceased, but then resumed as before. In the second year of Xianheng another edict declared: "The households of officials all belong to the gentry; on public roads, how can there be no screening at all?

sentences.zh: 比來多著帷帽，遂棄羃䍦，曾不乘車，別坐簷子。

translations.literal: Recently many have worn weimao hats and thus abandoned mili veils, not even riding in carriages but instead sitting separately in sedan chairs.
translations.idiomatic: Recently many have worn weimao hats and abandoned mili veils, not even riding in carriages but instead sitting separately in sedan chairs.

sentences.zh: 遞相仿效，浸成風俗，過為輕率，深失禮容。

translations.literal: People imitated one another in turn until it soaked into custom, becoming excessively careless and deeply losing proper ceremonial bearing.
translations.idiomatic: People copied one another until the practice soaked into custom, becoming excessively careless and deeply at odds with proper ceremonial bearing.

sentences.zh: 前者已令漸改，如聞猶未止息。

translations.literal: Previously an order was already given for gradual reform, but I hear it has still not ceased.
translations.idiomatic: An order for gradual reform had already been issued, yet I hear the practice has still not ceased.

sentences.zh: 又命婦朝謁，或將馳駕車，既入禁門，有虧肅敬。

translations.literal: Moreover, when titled ladies attended court audience, some would drive fast in carriages; once they entered the forbidden gate, this impaired solemn respect.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, when titled ladies attended court, some drove at speed in carriages; once they entered the forbidden gate, this impaired solemn respect.

sentences.zh: 此並乖於儀式，理須禁斷，自今已後，勿使更然。

translations.literal: All of this departs from ritual form and ought by right to be forbidden; from now on, do not let it happen again.
translations.idiomatic: All of this departs from ritual form and must be forbidden; from now on it must not be allowed to continue.

sentences.zh: 」則天之後，帷帽大行，羃䍦漸息。

translations.literal: After Zetian, weimao hats became widespread and mili veils gradually ceased.
translations.idiomatic: After Empress Zetian's reign, weimao hats became widespread and mili veils gradually fell out of use.

sentences.zh: 中宗即位，宮禁寬弛，公私婦人，無復冪䍦之制。

translations.literal: When Zhongzong ascended the throne, palace restrictions were relaxed, and among public and private women there was no longer any mili-veil regulation.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhongzong ascended the throne, palace restrictions were relaxed, and among women in public and private life the mili-veil rule was no longer observed.

sentences.zh: 開元初，從駕宮人騎馬者，皆著胡帽，靚妝露面，無復障蔽。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kaiyuan, palace women who rode horses in the imperial retinue all wore foreign hats, made up beautifully with faces exposed, no longer screened.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Kaiyuan, palace women who rode in the imperial retinue all wore foreign hats, made up beautifully with faces exposed and no longer screened.

sentences.zh: 士庶之家，又相仿效，帷帽之制，絕不行用。

translations.literal: Gentry and common households again imitated one another, and the weimao regulation ceased entirely to be used.
translations.idiomatic: Gentry and common households copied the fashion again, and the weimao rule fell completely out of use.

sentences.zh: 俄又露髻馳騁，或有著丈夫衣服靴衫，而尊卑內外，斯一貫矣。
