translations.literal: Soon they also rode with hair exposed, and some wore men's clothes, boots, and jackets; noble and base, inside and outside, became one continuous practice.
translations.idiomatic: Soon women were riding with hair exposed, and some wore men's clothes, boots, and jackets; by then noble and common, inside and outside the court, had become one undifferentiated fashion.

sentences.zh: 奚車，契丹塞外用之，開元、天寶中漸至京城。

translations.literal: Xi carts were used beyond the frontier by the Khitan; in Kaiyuan and Tianbao they gradually reached the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Xi carts were used by the Khitan beyond the frontier and gradually reached the capital during Kaiyuan and Tianbao.

sentences.zh: 兜籠，巴蜀婦人所用，今乾元已來，蕃將多著勳於朝，兜籠易於擔負，京城奚車、兜籠、代于車輿矣。

translations.literal: Doulong carrying frames were used by women of Ba and Shu; from Qianyuan onward frontier generals often wore their honors at court, and doulong frames were easy to carry; in the capital xi carts and doulong frames replaced carriages and sedan chairs.
translations.idiomatic: Doulong carrying frames were used by women of Ba and Shu; from Qianyuan onward frontier generals often wore their honors at court, and doulong frames were easy to carry; in the capital, xi carts and doulong frames replaced carriages and sedan chairs.

sentences.zh: 武德來，婦人著履，規制亦重，又有線靴。

translations.literal: Since Wude, women wore shoes; the regulations were also heavy, and there were also thread boots.
translations.idiomatic: Since Wude women had worn shoes, and the regulations governing them were strict; there were also thread boots.

sentences.zh: 開元來，婦人例著線鞋，取輕妙便於事，侍兒乃著履。

translations.literal: Since Kaiyuan, women generally wore thread shoes, taken for lightness and convenience in action; only attendants wore shoes.
translations.idiomatic: Since Kaiyuan women had generally worn thread shoes, chosen for lightness and convenience; only attendants wore shoes.

sentences.zh: 臧獲賤伍者皆服襴衫。

translations.literal: Bondservants and menials all wore lanshan tunics.
translations.idiomatic: Bondservants and menials all wore lanshan tunics.

sentences.zh: 太常樂尚胡曲，貴人禦饌，盡供胡食，士女皆竟衣胡服，故有范陽羯胡之亂，兆于好尚遠矣。

translations.literal: The Music Bureau favored foreign tunes; nobles at imperial banquets all served foreign food; gentlemen and women all competed in wearing foreign dress; hence the Fan-Yang Jie barbarian rebellion—the omen lay in favored fashions long before.
translations.idiomatic: The Music Bureau favored foreign tunes, nobles at imperial banquets served foreign food, and gentlemen and women vied in wearing foreign dress; the Fan-Yang rebellion had its omen in these favored fashions long before.

sentences.zh: 太極元年，左司郎中唐紹上疏曰：

translations.literal: First year of Taiji, Left Department Director Tang Shao submitted a memorial saying:
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Taiji, Tang Shao, Director of the Left Department, submitted a memorial saying:

sentences.zh: 臣聞王公已下，送終明器等物，具標甲令，品秩高下，各有節文。

translations.literal: Your subject has heard that from princes and dukes down, objects for funeral rites and spirit vessels are fully marked out in the primary code, and high and low rank each have their own regulations.
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that for princes and dukes down to common officials, objects for funeral rites and spirit vessels are fully prescribed in the primary code, with regulations differing according to rank.

sentences.zh: 孔子曰，明器者，備物而不可用，以芻靈者善，為俑者不仁。

translations.literal: Confucius said: spirit vessels prepare objects but cannot be used; using straw effigies is good, making figurines is unkind.
translations.idiomatic: Confucius said that spirit vessels represent objects but are not meant for use; using straw effigies is good, but making figurines is unkind.

sentences.zh: 傳曰，俑者，謂有面目機發，似于生人也。

translations.literal: The commentary says: figurines mean those with faces and moving parts, resembling living people.
translations.idiomatic: The commentary says that figurines are those with faces and moving parts, resembling living people.

sentences.zh: 以此而葬，殆將於殉，故曰不仁。

translations.literal: To bury with these is nearly akin to human sacrifice; hence it is called unkind.
translations.idiomatic: To bury with such objects is nearly akin to human sacrifice; that is why it is called unkind.

sentences.zh: 近者王公百官，競為厚葬，偶人像馬，雕飾如生，徒以眩耀路人，本不因心致禮。

translations.literal: Recently princes, dukes, and officials have competed in lavish burial; figurines, images, and horses are carved and ornamented as if alive, merely to dazzle passersby, not from the heart to perform ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Recently princes, dukes, and officials have competed in lavish burial, with figurines, images, and horses carved and ornamented as if alive, merely to dazzle passersby rather than from sincere ritual intent.

sentences.zh: 更相扇慕，破產傾資，風俗流行，遂下兼士庶。

translations.literal: They incited and admired one another, ruined families and exhausted fortunes; the custom spread until it reached down to gentry and commoners alike.
translations.idiomatic: They incited and admired one another, ruined families and exhausted fortunes, and the custom spread until it reached gentry and commoners alike.

sentences.zh: 若無禁制，奢侈日增。

translations.literal: If there is no prohibition, extravagance will increase daily.
translations.idiomatic: Without prohibition, extravagance will increase daily.

sentences.zh: 望諸王公已下，送葬明器，皆依令式，並陳於墓所，不得衢路行。

translations.literal: I hope that from princes and dukes down, spirit vessels for burial may all follow the code and regulations, be displayed only at the tomb site, and not be carried along public roads.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that from princes and dukes down, burial spirit vessels all follow the code and regulations, be displayed only at the tomb site, and not be carried along public roads.

sentences.zh: 又士庶親迎之儀，備諸辨禮，所以承宗廟，事舅姑，當須昏以為期，詰朝謁見。

translations.literal: Moreover, the ceremony of gentry and commoners receiving the bride is fully provided in the marriage rites, for inheriting the ancestral temple and serving parents-in-law; the wedding ought to be set for evening, with an audience the next morning.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the ceremony by which gentry and commoners receive the bride is fully provided in the marriage rites, for inheriting the ancestral temple and serving parents-in-law; the wedding ought to be set for evening, with an audience the next morning.

sentences.zh: 往者下俚庸鄙，時有障車，邀其酒食，以為戲樂。

translations.literal: Formerly among the vulgar and lowly there was sometimes wedding road-blocking, inviting wine and food as sport and amusement.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly among the vulgar and lowly there was sometimes wedding road-blocking, in which people demanded wine and food as sport and amusement.

sentences.zh: 近日此風轉盛，上及王公，乃廣奏音樂，多集徒侶，遮擁道路，留滯淹時，邀致財物，動逾萬計。

translations.literal: Recently this fashion has grown stronger, reaching even princes and dukes; they broadly perform music, gather many followers, block and crowd the roads, delay for long periods, and solicit goods, often exceeding ten thousand in value.
translations.idiomatic: Recently this fashion has grown stronger, reaching even princes and dukes; they perform music on a grand scale, gather large followings, block and crowd the roads, delay for long periods, and solicit gifts, often exceeding ten thousand in value.

sentences.zh: 遂使障車禮貺，過於聘財，歌舞喧嘩，殊非助感。

translations.literal: Thus wedding road-blocking gifts exceed betrothal wealth, and singing and dancing in noisy clamor are wholly unsuited to aiding solemn feeling.
translations.idiomatic: Thus wedding road-blocking gifts exceed betrothal wealth, and noisy singing and dancing do nothing to foster solemn feeling.

sentences.zh: 即虧名教，實蠹風猷，違紊禮經，須加節制。

translations.literal: This immediately damages moral teaching, truly harms proper custom, and violates and confuses the ritual canon; restraint must be added.
translations.idiomatic: This damages moral teaching, truly harms proper custom, and violates the ritual canon; restraint must be imposed.

sentences.zh: 望請婚姻家障車者，並須禁斷。

translations.literal: I hope and request that wedding road-blocking by marriage households all be forbidden.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that wedding road-blocking by marriage households be entirely forbidden.

sentences.zh: 其有犯者，有廕家請准犯名教例附簿，無廕人決杖六十，仍各科本罪。

translations.literal: Those who violate it: households with hereditary privilege should, according to the precedent for offenses against moral teaching, be entered in the register; those without privilege should be sentenced to sixty strokes of the rod, and each still punished according to the underlying offense.
translations.idiomatic: Violators with hereditary privilege should, according to the precedent for offenses against moral teaching, be entered in the register; those without privilege should receive sixty strokes of the rod, and each should still be punished for the underlying offense.
